5	
6	# Contributing
7	
8	This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
9	FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
10	firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
11	rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
12	alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
13	owner** before you open it.
14	
15	## Roles
16	
17	Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
18	the people who write ours.
19	
20	- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
21	  chip model was partly written from the GPL Felucca firmware's hardware
22	  layer. Builds the test harness and writes `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only
23	  (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols), never code or code structure,
24	  each fact citing a non-GPL source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
25	- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
26	  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
27	  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
28	  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
29	  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.
30	
31	- **Auditor (exposed to the GPL firmwares).** A third role, only for a
32	  failed similarity audit (docs/AUDIT.md, "When the audit fails"). The owner
33	  starts one; it works in a folder of its own set up with
34	  `tools/auditor-setup.sh` (settings `config/claude/auditor.json`), and may
35	  read the flagged GPL target files and our code. It writes only a finding
36	  in `audit/findings/`, in general terms (which of our files, the scores,
37	  the conclusion; never target code). It never writes firmware, the spec or
38	  the harness, then or in any later session. Its transcript holds GPL
39	  source, so it is **never archived in this repository**: it goes to the
40	  owner's private repository `small-beeps-audit` (created, with the
41	  owner's approval, when the first auditor session runs), committed there
42	  with an OpenTimestamps proof, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records the session's
43	  ID, the transcript's SHA-256 and that repository's commit.
44	
45	Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
46	and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
47	sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
48	EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.
49	
50	## Clean-room rules
51	
52	### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes
53	
54	- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
55	  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
56	- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
57	- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
58	  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
59	- any other FM-1 firmware source;
60	- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
61	  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
62	- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
63	  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
64	  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
65	  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
66	  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
67	  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
68	  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
69	  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
70	  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
71	  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
72	- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com.
73	
74	`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
75	this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together).
76	
77	### Firmware side may use
78	
79	Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
80	was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:
81	
82	- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
83	  source);
84	- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
85	  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
86	- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
87	  update-protocol documents only. Fetch single documents by URL; never clone
88	  it (a clone puts its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
89	- public datasheets;
90	- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
91	  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
92	- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
93	  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.
94	
95	### Barriers
96	
97	- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
98	  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
99	  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
100	  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
101	  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
102	  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
103	  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
104	  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
105	- **Records in a clean folder.** Each record on the `records` branch also
106	  keeps the harness's own test results and the hashes of their outputs.
107	  Records before SR-1-SR-2 also keep the spec experiments' outputs (memory
108	  dumps, captures, audio); since then a record keeps only their names and
109	  SHA-256 (`spec-experiments.sha256`), and older records stay as they are.
110	  Clean sessions never fetch the records branch wholesale (no `git archive`, checkout or
111	  lazy fetch of a whole record or of the branch): they fetch only named
112	  files of the firmware's own records, `report.json`, `report.md` and
113	  named logs under `logs/`, one path at a time. `tools/clean-update.sh`
114	  also stops if a file under a `harness/` or `spec-experiments/` folder,
115	  or under the excluded folders, is in `.git` through any branch, the
116	  records branch included (since M1, after a wholesale fetch brought 17
117	  such outputs into a clean folder; docs/EXPOSURE.md).
118	  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
119	  `config/claude/spec.json`.
120	- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
121	  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
122	- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
123	  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
124	  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
125	  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
126	  non-zero if they differ.
127	- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
128	  of every session, before anything else:
129	  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
130	     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
131	     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
132	     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
133	     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
134	     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
135	  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
136	  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
137	  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.
138	
139	### Spec-side text discipline
140	
141	What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
142	and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
143	sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
144	the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
145	titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
146	`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
147	changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
148	addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
149	comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
150	results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
151	`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
152	occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
153	by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
154	on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
155	term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
156	(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
157	door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
158	positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.
159	
160	## Commit messages
161	
162	Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
163	it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):
164	
165	```
166	<area>: <what changed, one line>
167	
168	What:    what this commit does
169	Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
170	How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
171	Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
172	Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
173	Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
174	```
175	
176	- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
177	  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
178	- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
179	- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
180	  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
181	  the agent; the owner is the committer.
182	- Small commits: one idea each.
183	- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
184	  carries the sections.
185	
186	`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).
187	
188	## Pull requests and merging
189	
190	- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
191	  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
192	  links to the CI run and the record).
193	- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
194	- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
195	  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
196	  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
197	  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
198	- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
199	  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main, and the similarity
200	  audit's report beside it (`records/<sha>/audit/`) only by
201	  `.github/workflows/audit.yml`'s record job (docs/AUDIT.md). Both use the
202	  `records` environment's deploy key.
203	- **Performance budgets** (`config/budgets.json`, R-PERF-1) are raised, or
204	  moved to the next milestone's, only by a pull request of their own that
205	  says why in the What/Why/How/Result sections and changes nothing else.
206	  When CI's performance summary shows an improvement of more than 3%
207	  (R-PERF-2), say so in the pull request's Result.
208	- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
209	  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
210	  SBOM.
211	
212	### Merge policy and its history
213	
214	- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
215	  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
216	  with GitHub's key instead.
217	- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
218	  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
219	  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
220	  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
221	- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
222	  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.
223	
224	What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
225	by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
226	button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
227	The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
228	(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
229	the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
230	as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
231	run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
232	is still written.
233	
234	## Rulesets
235	
236	Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):
237	
238	- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
239	  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
240	  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
241	  role).
242	- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
243	  pushes; no bypass.
244	- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
245	  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
246	  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
247	- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
248	  bypass.
249	
250	Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging

# Contributing

This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
owner** before you open it.

## Roles

Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
the people who write ours.

- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
  chip model was partly written from the GPL Felucca firmware's hardware
  layer. Builds the test harness and writes `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only
  (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols), never code or code structure,
  each fact citing a non-GPL source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.

- **Auditor (exposed to the GPL firmwares).** A third role, only for a
  failed similarity audit (docs/AUDIT.md, "When the audit fails"). The owner
  starts one; it works in a folder of its own set up with
  `tools/auditor-setup.sh` (settings `config/claude/auditor.json`), and may
  read the flagged GPL target files and our code. It writes only a finding
  in `audit/findings/`, in general terms (which of our files, the scores,
  the conclusion; never target code). It never writes firmware, the spec or
  the harness, then or in any later session. Its transcript holds GPL
  source, so it is **never archived in this repository**: it goes to the
  owner's private repository `small-beeps-audit` (created, with the
  owner's approval, when the first auditor session runs), committed there
  with an OpenTimestamps proof, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records the session's
  ID, the transcript's SHA-256 and that repository's commit.

Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.

## Clean-room rules

### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes

- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
- any other FM-1 firmware source;
- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com.

`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together).

### Firmware side may use

Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:

- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
  source);
- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
  update-protocol documents only. Fetch single documents by URL; never clone
  it (a clone puts its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
- public datasheets;
- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

### Barriers

- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
- **Records in a clean folder.** Each record on the `records` branch also
  keeps the harness's own test results and the hashes of their outputs.
  Records before SR-1-SR-2 also keep the spec experiments' outputs (memory
  dumps, captures, audio); since then a record keeps only their names and
  SHA-256 (`spec-experiments.sha256`), and older records stay as they are.
  Clean sessions never fetch the records branch wholesale (no `git archive`, checkout or
  lazy fetch of a whole record or of the branch): they fetch only named
  files of the firmware's own records, `report.json`, `report.md` and
  named logs under `logs/`, one path at a time. `tools/clean-update.sh`
  also stops if a file under a `harness/` or `spec-experiments/` folder,
  or under the excluded folders, is in `.git` through any branch, the
  records branch included (since M1, after a wholesale fetch brought 17
  such outputs into a clean folder; docs/EXPOSURE.md).
  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
  `config/claude/spec.json`.
- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
  non-zero if they differ.
- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
  of every session, before anything else:
  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.

### Spec-side text discipline

What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.

## Commit messages

Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):

```
<area>: <what changed, one line>

What:    what this commit does
Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
```

- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
  the agent; the owner is the committer.
- Small commits: one idea each.
- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
  carries the sections.

`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).

## Pull requests and merging

- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
  links to the CI run and the record).
- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main, and the similarity
  audit's report beside it (`records/<sha>/audit/`) only by
  `.github/workflows/audit.yml`'s record job (docs/AUDIT.md). Both use the
  `records` environment's deploy key.
- **Performance budgets** (`config/budgets.json`, R-PERF-1) are raised, or
  moved to the next milestone's, only by a pull request of their own that
  says why in the What/Why/How/Result sections and changes nothing else.
  When CI's performance summary shows an improvement of more than 3%
  (R-PERF-2), say so in the pull request's Result.
- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
  SBOM.

### Merge policy and its history

- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
  with GitHub's key instead.
- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.

What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
is still written.

## Rulesets

Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):

- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
  role).
- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
  pushes; no bypass.
- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
  bypass.

Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging
off).

Set up on 2026-10-22 by session M0a, with the owner's approval, through the
GitHub API:

| What | ID or fingerprint |
|------|-------------------|
| Ruleset `main` | 25612787 (required check `ci` from GitHub Actions; no bypass since 2026-10-22, before that the repository admin role) |
| Ruleset `records-history` | 25612788 |
| Ruleset `records-writer` | 25612790 (bypass: deploy keys) |
| Ruleset `milestone-tags` | 25612791 |
| Environment `records` | deployments from `main` only; secret `RECORDS_DEPLOY_KEY` |
| Deploy key "records workflow (records branch writer)" | 167260041, write access, ED25519 `SHA256:Od9RfSkzLwqLYSZRf1X7jEdcLhty0n1ISgQ+ec43Dkk` |

folder, piped into the environment secret without being printed, and
deleted. To rotate it: make a new pair, replace the secret, add the new
public key, delete the old key.

   `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "small-beeps signing" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing`
2. Tell git to sign with it:

4. On GitHub: Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → Key type
   **Signing Key**, and paste the `.pub` contents.
5. Tag a milestone: `git tag -s mN -m "mN"`, then `git push origin mN`.
6. Check: `git tag -v mN` shows "Good "git" signature", and GitHub shows the
   tag as **Verified**.

## Licences

  matched ignoring case) and in the repository secret `PRIVATE_TERMS`, which

- **The check** `tools/check-private.py` (C-PRIVATE, R-PUB-3) scans every
  tracked file and every commit message, and the pre-commit and commit-msg
  hooks scan staged files and the message (`tools/install-hooks.sh` turns

6	# Contributing
7	
8	This repository is a clean-room, MIT-licensed base firmware for the M-VAVE
9	FM-1 pocket synthesizer (JieLi AC791N). The FM-1's existing community
10	firmwares are GPL-licensed; ours must be provably independent of them. The
11	rules below make that provable. Everyone follows them, people and agents
12	alike. If you are unsure whether something is allowed, **stop and ask the
13	owner** before you open it.
14	
15	## Roles
16	
17	Clean-room work separates the people who have seen the protected code from
18	the people who write ours.
19	
20	- **Spec side (exposed).** May read the F-Emulator emulator's source, whose
21	  chip model was partly written from the GPL Felucca firmware's hardware
22	  layer. Builds the test harness and writes `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`: facts only
23	  (addresses, bits, pins, timings, protocols), never code or code structure,
24	  each fact citing a non-GPL source where one exists. Never writes firmware.
25	- **Firmware side (clean).** Writes the firmware. Reads only
26	  `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the JieLi SDK (Apache-2.0), FM-1-RE's hardware
27	  documents (WTFPL), public datasheets, and results of its own black-box
28	  experiments. Uses the harness only as a command-line tool, and never opens
29	  `vendor/emulator/` or `harness/` source.
30	
31	- **Auditor (exposed to the GPL firmwares).** A third role, only for a
32	  failed similarity audit (docs/AUDIT.md, "When the audit fails"). The owner
33	  starts one; it works in a folder of its own set up with
34	  `tools/auditor-setup.sh` (settings `config/claude/auditor.json`), and may
35	  read the flagged GPL target files and our code. It writes only a finding
36	  in `audit/findings/`, in general terms (which of our files, the scores,
37	  the conclusion; never target code). It never writes firmware, the spec or
38	  the harness, then or in any later session. Its transcript holds GPL
39	  source, so it is **never archived in this repository**: it goes to the
40	  owner's private repository `small-beeps-audit` (created, with the
41	  owner's approval, when the first auditor session runs), committed there
42	  with an OpenTimestamps proof, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records the session's
43	  ID, the transcript's SHA-256 and that repository's commit.
44	
45	Every person and every session is recorded in docs/EXPOSURE.md with its role
46	and exposure, before it does any work. A firmware-side person or session that
47	sees forbidden material becomes spec side from that moment: record it in
48	EXPOSURE.md at once, and stop writing firmware.
49	
50	## Clean-room rules
51	
52	### Firmware side never opens, fetches, searches or quotes
53	
54	- hugelton/Felucca and every fork or firmware built on it (Felucca Salt,
55	  Felucca 8 Patterns, Hortator, GHOULBOX, Melodee, Skiff, ...);
56	- zvenson/dinghy and anything built on it;
57	- the F-Emulator / fm1-emu repository's `fm1-sid/` directory, its
58	  `probes/lcdtest.c`, and its emulator source (`crates/`);
59	- any other FM-1 firmware source;
60	- M-VAVE's stock firmware and any disassembly or function database of it
61	  (including AL-255/FM-1-RE's `firmware-images/` and disassembly material);
62	- in this repository: `vendor/emulator/` and `harness/` source (spec side's
63	  work), and spec-side session transcripts (`sessions/spec/`), which
64	  contain emulator source. A clean folder never has their contents, not
65	  even in `.git`: clean sessions run with git's lazy fetching off
66	  (`GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1`, from `config/claude/clean.json`), so a history
67	  command that would need them (`git log -p`, `git show`, `git diff`
68	  across commits) fails instead of downloading them. Give such commands a
69	  pathspec that leaves the three folders out, and update the folder only
70	  with `tools/clean-update.sh`. People working in a clean folder by hand
71	  set `GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH=1` in their shell too;
72	- the sites hugelton.github.io and thefirmwarehub.com.
73	
74	`tools/check-transcripts.py` checks every archived clean-side session against
75	this list (its `FORBIDDEN` table mirrors it; change both together).
76	
77	### Firmware side may use
78	
79	Log every use in PROVENANCE.md (an ID, the source, what was learned, where it
80	was used) and name the ID in the commit's `Sources:` field:
81	
82	- `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, once it exists (each fact there already cites its own
83	  source);
84	- JieLi's AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), Apache-2.0:
85	  headers, register definitions, drivers. Not its prebuilt libraries;
86	- AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL): its hardware, memory-map, boot-chain and
87	  update-protocol documents only. Fetch single documents by URL; never clone
88	  it (a clone puts its firmware images and disassembly material on disk);
89	- public datasheets;
90	- our own experiments: test programs run in the emulator, observed only
91	  through the harness: `tools/fwtest`, whose manual is docs/HARNESS.md;
92	- answers to spec requests (docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md), which arrive as facts
93	  in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.
94	
95	### Barriers
96	
97	- **Clean folder.** `tools/clean-setup.sh [DIR]` creates the clean working
98	  folder: a blob-less clone with a sparse checkout that leaves out
99	  `vendor/emulator/`, `harness/` and `sessions/spec/` (and marks them
100	  `-diff` for history commands), plus the Claude Code settings in
101	  `config/claude/clean.json`, which deny reading those paths, fetching the
102	  forbidden sites and cloning the forbidden repositories, and turn git's
103	  lazy fetching off. `tools/clean-update.sh` updates a clean folder and
104	  checks nothing excluded arrived; C-CLEAN-FOLDER tests all of this in CI.
105	- **Records in a clean folder.** Each record on the `records` branch also
106	  keeps the harness's own test results and the hashes of their outputs.
107	  Records before SR-1-SR-2 also keep the spec experiments' outputs (memory
108	  dumps, captures, audio); since then a record keeps only their names and
109	  SHA-256 (`spec-experiments.sha256`), and older records stay as they are.
110	  Clean sessions never fetch the records branch wholesale (no `git archive`, checkout or
111	  lazy fetch of a whole record or of the branch): they fetch only named
112	  files of the firmware's own records, `report.json`, `report.md` and
113	  named logs under `logs/`, one path at a time. `tools/clean-update.sh`
114	  also stops if a file under a `harness/` or `spec-experiments/` folder,
115	  or under the excluded folders, is in `.git` through any branch, the
116	  records branch included (since M1, after a wholesale fetch brought 17
117	  such outputs into a clean folder; docs/EXPOSURE.md).
118	  `tools/spec-setup.sh [DIR]` does the same for spec side with
119	  `config/claude/spec.json`.
120	- **Deny lists only grow.** Never remove or loosen an entry in
121	  `config/claude/*.json`. Check C-DENY-LISTS fails if one is dropped.
122	- **Session banner.** Both configs run `tools/session-banner.sh` on every
123	  SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact). It prints the role,
124	  `claude --version`, the SHA-256 of `.claude/settings.json` and of the
125	  committed config, and the UTC time, and prints `CONFIG MISMATCH` and exits
126	  non-zero if they differ.
127	- **Session transcripts.** Each milestone gets a fresh session. At the start
128	  of every session, before anything else:
129	  1. archive the previous session's transcript with
130	     `python3 tools/archive-session.py <transcript.jsonl> --role <role>`
131	     (it redacts secrets and private paths, writes the copy to
132	     `sessions/<role>/` and a note beside it). A spec session may archive
133	     the previous session of either role; a clean session archives only
134	     clean sessions and never opens `sessions/spec/` (sessions/README.md);
135	  2. run `python3 tools/check-transcripts.py`;
136	  3. add this session's entry to docs/EXPOSURE.md.
137	  A session never archives its own live transcript; the next one does.
138	
139	### Spec-side text discipline
140	
141	What the spec side learns from emulator source leaves `vendor/emulator/`
142	and `harness/` only through two doors: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` (facts only, each
143	sourced) and `docs/HARNESS.md` (the harness as a black box). Everything else
144	the firmware side can read, so spec-side commit messages, pull request
145	titles and descriptions, and every file outside those two folders and
146	`sessions/spec/` (docs, tools, tests, records, release notes) describe what
147	changed in general terms, never emulator internals: no register names,
148	addresses, struct or function names, or code excerpts. Such detail goes in
149	comments inside `harness/`. CI logs and records from harness runs show
150	results (pass/fail, hashes, images, numbers), never emulator source.
151	`tools/check-emulator-terms.py` (C-SEP-TERMS) looks for identifiers that
152	occur only in `vendor/emulator/` in all of those places and reports a hit
153	by place and hash, never the word; run it (with `--show`, in a spec folder)
154	on your commit messages before you push. People review the two doors, so a
155	term that occurs in either of them as merged on main is accepted everywhere
156	(read from main's commit, never the working tree: a term a branch adds to a
157	door is still a hit until that change has merged). Other reviewed false
158	positives are listed by hash in `config/emulator-terms-reviewed.json`.
159	
160	## Commit messages
161	
162	Every commit follows `.gitmessage` (run `tools/install-hooks.sh` once to make
163	it git's template and turn on the commit-msg hook):
164	
165	```
166	<area>: <what changed, one line>
167	
168	What:    what this commit does
169	Why:     the reason (the milestone and requirement IDs it serves)
170	How:     the approach, and anything tried and rejected
171	Result:  what the author saw when testing (the CI record is the authoritative result)
172	Sources: PROVENANCE IDs used (or "none")
173	Exposure: the author's role and exposure (e.g. "firmware side, none")
174	```
175	
176	- `<area>` is lower-case: `docs`, `tools`, `ci`, `firmware`, `vendor`,
177	  `config`, `sessions`, and so on.
178	- A field may continue on following lines, indented.
179	- Agent-written commits end with the trailers `Model: <exact model ID>` and
180	  `Claude-Session: <session URL>` (and `Co-Authored-By:`). Their author is
181	  the agent; the owner is the committer.
182	- Small commits: one idea each.
183	- Merge commits are exempt from the template; the pull request they merge
184	  carries the sections.
185	
186	`tools/check-commit-msg.py` enforces this in the hook and in CI (C-COMMIT-MSG).
187	
188	## Pull requests and merging
189	
190	- Agents and contributors commit **unsigned** on branches and open a pull
191	  request using `.github/pull_request_template.md` (the same sections, plus
192	  links to the CI run and the record).
193	- CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) must pass.
194	- The **owner merges with GitHub's merge button** ("Create a merge commit").
195	  GitHub commits and signs the merge commit as `web-flow` (shown as
196	  Verified) and records the owner as the pull request's `merged_by`. No
197	  squash or rebase merges, and nobody bypasses the rules.
198	- Records (`records/<sha>/` on the `records` branch) are written only by
199	  `.github/workflows/records.yml`, for pushes to main, and the similarity
200	  audit's report beside it (`records/<sha>/audit/`) only by
201	  `.github/workflows/audit.yml`'s record job (docs/AUDIT.md). Both use the
202	  `records` environment's deploy key.
203	- **Performance budgets** (`config/budgets.json`, R-PERF-1) are raised, or
204	  moved to the next milestone's, only by a pull request of their own that
205	  says why in the What/Why/How/Result sections and changes nothing else.
206	  When CI's performance summary shows an improvement of more than 3%
207	  (R-PERF-2), say so in the pull request's Result.
208	- Milestones end with a tag `mN`, signed by the owner with their SSH key
209	  (below), and a GitHub release with the build outputs, the record and an
210	  SBOM.
211	
212	### Merge policy and its history
213	
214	- **2026-10-21:** the owner first chose to sign every merge with their own
215	  SSH key, as the ruleset's only bypass actor, because GitHub's button signs
216	  with GitHub's key instead.
217	- **2026-10-22:** pull request #1 was merged with the button. Its merge
218	  commit `2fd28219` is signed by GitHub (`web-flow`, verified), and its
219	  record shows C-MERGE **FAIL** under the old rule ("committer is web-flow,
220	  not the owner"). The record stays as it is, and history is not rewritten.
221	- **2026-10-22:** the owner then chose button merges for good. The bypass
222	  was removed from the main ruleset, so the rules now apply to everyone.
223	
224	What a merge on main proves: GitHub's signature shows the commit was made
225	by GitHub on the owner's merge. `merged_by` shows the owner pressed the
226	button. The required `ci` check shows CI passed on exactly the merged head.
227	The records workflow re-checks all of this for every push to main
228	(C-MERGE): a merge commit, a verified signature, committer `web-flow` with
229	the pull request's `merged_by` the owner (or, for older merges, the owner
230	as committer), and its second parent the head of a pull request whose `ci`
231	run passed. Otherwise the record says **FAIL** for C-MERGE, and the record
232	is still written.
233	
234	## Rulesets
235	
236	Repository rulesets (Settings → Rules → Rulesets):
237	
238	- **main**: restrict deletions; block force pushes; require a pull request
239	  before merging (allowed merge method: merge only); require status checks to
240	  pass (the `ci` job); no bypass (until 2026-10-22: the repository admin
241	  role).
242	- **records-history** (branch `records`): restrict deletions; block force
243	  pushes; no bypass.
244	- **records-writer** (branch `records`): restrict creations; restrict
245	  updates; bypass list: deploy keys only. Together these make the records
246	  workflow's deploy key the only writer, and it can only add commits.
247	- **milestone-tags** (tags `m*`): restrict deletions; restrict updates; no
248	  bypass.
249	
250	Repository settings: allow merge commits only (squash and rebase merging
251	off).
252	
253	Set up on 2026-10-22 by session M0a, with the owner's approval, through the
254	GitHub API:
255	
256	| What | ID or fingerprint |
257	|------|-------------------|
258	| Ruleset `main` | 25612787 (required check `ci` from GitHub Actions; no bypass since 2026-10-22, before that the repository admin role) |
259	| Ruleset `records-history` | 25612788 |
260	| Ruleset `records-writer` | 25612790 (bypass: deploy keys) |
261	| Ruleset `milestone-tags` | 25612791 |
262	| Environment `records` | deployments from `main` only; secret `RECORDS_DEPLOY_KEY` |
263	| Deploy key "records workflow (records branch writer)" | 167260041, write access, ED25519 `SHA256:Od9RfSkzLwqLYSZRf1X7jEdcLhty0n1ISgQ+ec43Dkk` |
264	
265	The deploy key's private half was generated in the session's scratch
266	folder, piped into the environment secret without being printed, and
267	deleted. To rotate it: make a new pair, replace the secret, add the new
268	public key, delete the old key.
269	
270	## SSH signing for milestone tags (one-time setup, owner)
271	
272	1. Create a signing key (or reuse an SSH key you already have):
273	   `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "small-beeps signing" -f ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing`
274	2. Tell git to sign with it:
275	   ```sh
276	   git config --global gpg.format ssh
277	   git config --global user.signingkey ~/.ssh/id_ed25519_signing.pub
278	   git config --global tag.gpgSign true
279	   ```
280	   Leave `commit.gpgSign` off: merges are signed by GitHub's button.
281	3. Let git verify signatures locally: add a line
282	   `<your git email> <contents of id_ed25519_signing.pub>` to
283	   `~/.ssh/allowed_signers`, then
284	   `git config --global gpg.ssh.allowedSignersFile ~/.ssh/allowed_signers`.
285	4. On GitHub: Settings → SSH and GPG keys → New SSH key → Key type
286	   **Signing Key**, and paste the `.pub` contents.
287	5. Tag a milestone: `git tag -s mN -m "mN"`, then `git push origin mN`.
288	6. Check: `git tag -v mN` shows "Good "git" signature", and GitHub shows the
289	   tag as **Verified**.
290	
291	## Licences
292	
293	- Every file we write starts with an SPDX header:
294	  `SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT` and `SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98`.
295	  Files that can't carry one are covered in `REUSE.toml`.
296	- Vendored files keep their own licences (`vendor/*/LICENSE`, `NOTICE`).
297	- CI runs `reuse lint` and fails on any gap (C-REUSE).
298	- Never commit the toolchain or anything containing it (docs/TOOLCHAIN.md).
299	- Nothing secret ever goes in: no keys, tokens or private notes. The
300	  repository is public and history is never rewritten.
301	
302	## Privacy
303	
304	The repository is public. No committed file, commit message or pull request
305	text names the owner's username, real name, e-mail address, hostname or
306	local folder names, or a full local path: write paths relative to the
307	repository, or as `~/...` with the top folder shown as `<top>`. Anyone who
308	finds such a term in the repository tells the owner instead of repeating it.
309	
310	- **The terms** are kept by the owner, never in the repository: in the
311	  gitignored `tools/[REDACTED:host]` (one per line, `#` comments,
312	  matched ignoring case) and in the repository secret `PRIVATE_TERMS`, which
313	  CI passes to the check.
314	- **The check** `tools/check-private.py` (C-PRIVATE, R-PUB-3) scans every
315	  tracked file and every commit message, and the pre-commit and commit-msg
316	  hooks scan staged files and the message (`tools/install-hooks.sh` turns
317	  them on). A hit is reported by file and line only, never the term. CI
318	  fails when the secret is missing.
319	- **Records are scanned too** (since M1). Before a test record, an audit
320	  report or a C-MERGE re-check is hashed, uploaded or pushed, any file in
321	  it holding a term is withheld: deleted, and listed with the SHA-256 of
322	  the original in `WITHHELD.json`, which the record keeps (C-RECORD-PRIVATE).
323	  The original is not kept anywhere; the checks are deterministic, so it
324	  can be regenerated and matched to its hash. CI artifacts are kept 14 days.
325	- **Older records stay as they are.** A file under `sessions/` or
326	  `docs/prompts/` whose blob is identical to the same path at the base
327	  commit in `config/private-base` (the last main commit before the check)
328	  is exempt. This is decided from git's object hashes alone, so no session
329	  opens or lists the spec side's transcripts for it, and the check prints
330	  only how many files it exempted per folder. Every file added or changed
331	  after the base is checked in full. Files that sessions keep editing get no
332	  exemption: their current text is redacted instead (`docs/EXPOSURE.md` was,
333	  on 2026-10-22), and git history keeps the originals.
334	- **Archived transcripts** are redacted by `tools/archive-session.py`: the
335	  username anywhere it appears, the local top-level folder as `<top>`, and
336	  every private term.
337	
338	## Low profile (for now)
339	
340	The repository is public but unpromoted. In its name, description and topics,
341	and in README.md, never use these quiet words: **FM-1, M-VAVE, JieLi, synth,
342	firmware** (any spelling or case; `tools/check-low-profile.py` has the
343	patterns). Don't link the repository from anywhere, star it, fork it or
344	announce it. Everything else in the repository stays complete and truthful.
345	docs/GOING-PUBLIC.md says how this ends.

# Session transcripts

Every agent session that works on this repository is kept here as evidence.
A session's transcript is the full record of what it read, searched,
fetched, ran and wrote, so anyone can check that a firmware-side (clean)
session never touched forbidden material (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Clean-room
rules"; R-CLEAN-1, R-CLEAN-3).

## Folders, and who archives whom

- `clean/`: firmware-side (clean) sessions.
- `spec/`: spec-side sessions. Their transcripts contain emulator source,
  so `tools/clean-setup.sh` leaves this folder out of clean folders, and the
  clean settings deny reading it.

A **spec** session may archive the previous session of either role. A
**clean** session archives only clean sessions, and never opens, lists or
searches anything under `spec/`. When the previous session was spec side
and the next is clean, the clean session leaves it for the next spec
session to archive.

An **auditor** session (CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles") is never archived here:
its transcript holds GPL source, so it goes to the owner's private
repository, and docs/EXPOSURE.md records its ID, SHA-256 and that
repository's commit. `tools/check-transcripts.py` fails on any transcript
outside `clean/` and `spec/`.

## Files

Each role folder holds:

- `<date>-<role>-<id>.jsonl`: the session's Claude Code transcript, one JSON
  entry per line, as Claude Code wrote it under `~/.claude/projects/`, with
  secrets and private details redacted. `<date>` is the UTC date of its first
  entry, `<role>` is `clean` or `spec`, and `<id>` is the Claude Code session
  ID.
- `<same name>.REDACTIONS.md`: what was redacted (kind and count), with the
  SHA-256 of the original and of the redacted copy. The owner keeps the
  originals, so a redacted copy can be matched to its original if that is
  ever challenged.
- `<same name>.subagents/`: transcripts of subagents the session started, if
  any.

## How they get here

A session never archives itself, because its transcript is still being
written. The **next** session, before doing anything else, runs:

```sh
python3 tools/archive-session.py ~/.claude/projects/<project>/<id>.jsonl --role <role> \
    --archived-by "<this session's id>"        # writes to sessions/<role>/
python3 tools/check-transcripts.py
```

and commits the result.

# M3: keys, encoders, pot, LEDs

## 0. Start safely

1. Banner OK; tools/clean-update.sh ends with "no spec-side files on disk or in .git" (stop on STOP); tools/[REDACTED:host] exists (don't open it). Run every git command in this folder with lazy fetching off, as the tools do.

## 1. Scope

Read every control on the panel and drive its LEDs, from HARDWARE-SPEC.md, the SDK headers and the allowed FM-1-RE documents:
- **Keys and buttons:** scan the matrix, debounce, and report presses and releases with timestamps; handle several held at once, and say in the design notes what the matrix can and can't tell apart.
- **Encoders:** decode direction and steps reliably at any speed fwtest can produce; optional acceleration, documented.

<!--

# Hardware spec

What the spec side knows about the board, and about how fwtest presents it,
as numbered facts. It is the firmware side's only window onto that knowledge
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"). It holds facts, never code, and never how any
firmware or the emulator is written: each entry states a property of the
hardware, or a requirement it imposes, and leaves the design of the code to
the firmware side.

Written by session M0c (spec side), 2026-10-22. Ask for anything missing
through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md. Open spec requests at the time of writing:
none. Session SR-1-SR-2 (spec side, 2026-10-22) added sections 9 to 11 for
SR-1 and SR-2, which are answered in part; what stays open is Q-2, Q-13
and Q-14.

## How to read it

Every fact is an entry:

- **ID**: `HW-n`. IDs are never reused or renumbered. A corrected fact gets a
  new ID, and the old entry stays, marked superseded.
- **Fact**: the property or requirement. "On the chip" means the AC791N on
  the FM-1; "in fwtest" means how fwtest presents it (docs/HARNESS.md). Where
  an entry says neither, it holds for both as far as the sources go.
- **Sources**: as precisely as possible (the keys are under "Sources" below).
- **Standing**:
  - **confirmed**: an independent source agrees: the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE's
    documents, a datasheet, the panel sources, or a spec-side black-box
    experiment in fwtest (E-n). An experiment confirms how fwtest behaves,
    not how the chip behaves; the sources say which kind of confirmation it
    is.
  - **emulator-only**: the only source is the emulator model, which was
    partly written from GPL code. Rely on it in fwtest, but prefer to confirm
    it with your own black-box test.
  - **superseded by HW-n**: no longer true; see the newer entry.
- **Needed by**: the milestone that first needs it.

Numbers are hexadecimal with `0x`; registers are 32 bits wide and
little-endian unless an entry says otherwise. "Bit n" counts from bit 0, the
least significant. Register names are the JieLi SDK's.

## Sources

| Key | Source |
|-----|--------|
| SDK | JieLi AC79 SDK, `Jieli-Tech/fw-AC79_AIoT_SDK` (Gitee), commit `5fa84a9b2f723a5e9337ad79dc2ad741fc98fe2d`, Apache-2.0 (PROVENANCE P-2, P-10). `WL82.h` and `csfr.h` are vendored in `vendor/jieli-sdk/include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/`; the other files cited are at the same commit and path prefix. Line numbers refer to that commit. |
| RE | AL-255/FM-1-RE (GitHub, WTFPL), commit `ec832f281ca165a7d5e0722985f3acb1465046d5`: its hardware and boot documents `docs/reversing/01-hardware-map.md`, `docs/io/01-boot.md`, `docs/io/03-audio-dac.md`, `docs/io/08-display.md`, `docs/io/09-storage.md` (PROVENANCE P-9). Only their hardware facts are used here. |
| DS | Sitronix ST7789V datasheet, version 1.3 (2014-03), 316 pages, from `https://www.newhavendisplay.com/appnotes/datasheets/LCDs/ST7789V.pdf`, SHA-256 `8ecf0e43…5d04ca1` (PROVENANCE P-11). Page numbers as printed. |
| PANEL | The FM-1's printed panel labels, from two sources that agree: the owner's screenshot of the F-Emulator app's panel with its default labels, `docs/sources/panel-app-default-labels.png` (secondary: the app's drawing of the panel); and M-VAVE's product photo of the FM-1, `https://www.m-vave.com/images/products/fm-1.webp` on `https://www.m-vave.com/product.html?id=fm-1`, accessed 2026-10-22, SHA-256 `e610a746…df14b95`, not copied into this repository (PROVENANCE P-12). Only the printed labels are taken from them. The owner chose these two sources. |
| HARNESS | docs/HARNESS.md, fwtest's manual. It is the spec side's own description of fwtest, so it never confirms an entry on its own. |
| E-n | A spec-side black-box experiment: a small image run in fwtest (the pinned image, `config/fwtest-image`). Its result is stated in the entry. C-SPEC-EXPERIMENTS re-runs every one in CI, so a cited result that stops holding fails CI. |

---

## 6. Keys, encoders, the pot and LEDs (M3)

### HW-33: The key matrix's columns, in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest the matrix has 11 columns, selected through two cascaded
  8-bit shift registers with output latches: serial data on PA4, shift
  clock on PA3 (each rising edge shifts in one bit), latch clock on PA1 (a
  rising edge copies the 16 shifted bits to the outputs). The 16 bits go
  most significant first; output bit c drives column c (0-10; bits 11-15
  are not used). A column is selected while its bit is 0. The pins are
  bits of `JL_PORTA->OUT` (`0x00050000`) and need no set-up in fwtest.
  Whether the board is wired this way is Q-7.
- Sources: SDK `WL82.h` lines 252, 263 (`JL_PORTA`); E-6: a scan selecting
  one column at a time this way saw every key and encoder contact.
- Standing: confirmed (E-6)
- Needed by: M3

### HW-34: The key matrix's rows, in fwtest

What the spec side knows about the board, and about how fwtest presents it,
as numbered facts. It is the firmware side's only window onto that knowledge
(CONTRIBUTING.md, "Roles"). It holds facts, never code, and never how any
firmware or the emulator is written: each entry states a property of the
hardware, or a requirement it imposes, and leaves the design of the code to
the firmware side.

through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md. Open spec requests at the time of writing:
none. Session SR-1-SR-2 (spec side, 2026-10-22) added sections 9 to 11 for
SR-1 and SR-2, which are answered in part; what stays open is Q-2, Q-13
and Q-14.

## How to read it

Every fact is an entry:

- **ID**: `HW-n`. IDs are never reused or renumbered. A corrected fact gets a
  new ID, and the old entry stays, marked superseded.
- **Fact**: the property or requirement. "On the chip" means the AC791N on
  the FM-1; "in fwtest" means how fwtest presents it (docs/HARNESS.md). Where
  an entry says neither, it holds for both as far as the sources go.
- **Sources**: as precisely as possible (the keys are under "Sources" below).
- **Standing**:
  - **confirmed**: an independent source agrees: the JieLi SDK, FM-1-RE's
    documents, a datasheet, the panel sources, or a spec-side black-box
    experiment in fwtest (E-n). An experiment confirms how fwtest behaves,
    not how the chip behaves; the sources say which kind of confirmation it
    is.

    partly written from GPL code. Rely on it in fwtest, but prefer to confirm
    it with your own black-box test.
  - **superseded by HW-n**: no longer true; see the newer entry.
- **Needed by**: the milestone that first needs it.

Numbers are hexadecimal with `0x`; registers are 32 bits wide and
little-endian unless an entry says otherwise. "Bit n" counts from bit 0, the
least significant. Register names are the JieLi SDK's.

# fwtest: the harness, as a black box

`fwtest` runs a raw image on an emulated board for a given number of
emulated milliseconds, feeds it timed inputs, and saves what it did:
memory, the screen, the LEDs, the flash chip, the audio, instruction counts.
It is the firmware side's only window into the emulator, and this page is
its whole manual. It says what fwtest does, not how the emulator does it.
Facts about the chip itself (registers, pins, timings, the panel's layout)
belong in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`; ask for one through docs/SPEC-REQUESTS.md.

fwtest is a model. Where it and `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` disagree, the spec is the
authority on the hardware; report the difference as a spec request.

## Running it

The firmware side runs fwtest only through `tools/fwtest`, which runs the
published container image pinned by digest in `config/fwtest-image`
(R-SEP-3). It needs Docker; the image runs as linux/amd64 on any host.

```sh
tools/fwtest run out/build/app.bin --ms 100 --out out/t1 --ram 0x01c00000:64@end
tools/fwtest suite tests/fw/boot.suite --out out/suite
tools/fwtest version
tools/fwtest --image        # the pinned image reference
```

- Run it from the repository root. The current folder is mounted read-only,
  so every input path (image, script, flash file, golden folder, suite) must
  be inside it. `--out` is created and mounted writable on its own, and must
  be empty or not exist yet.
- The container has no network and runs as your user.
- After a run, `tools/fwtest` adds `runner.txt` to the output folder, naming
  the image it ran and whether it was the pinned one. A test record that
  used fwtest names that image; every record also notes the pinned image in
  its environment.

## The raw image

| Rule | Value |
|------|-------|
| Format | A flat binary: the bytes of the code window, from its first byte. No header, no ELF. |
| Load address | The image's first byte is at `0x02000000`, the start of the code window. Link it there. |
| Entry | Core 0 starts at `0x02000000`: the image's first instruction. |
| Size | 1 byte to 1 032 192 bytes (1 MiB less 16 KiB). |
| The flash chip | 1 MiB. Erased (all `0xFF`) unless `--flash FILE` gives its first bytes. The image is then written into it at offset `0x4000`, as an installed image sits. |
| Past the image | Reads in the code window after the image's last byte show the flash chip: window address `0x02000000 + n` shows chip offset `0x4000 + n`. Changes the image makes to the chip (erase, program) show through the window, also over the image's own bytes. |
| Writes to the window | Ignored (and listed as unmodelled accesses). |
| RAM | 1 MiB at `0x01C00000`, all zero at the start. Other memories, and what the real chip has: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| Core 0 at the start | User mode. Every register is 0, both stack pointers included (set your own stacks first), except `r0` = `0x01C7FC00`: a 64-byte block of zeros whose first word holds `0x01C7FC40`. |
| Core 1 | Does not run until the image releases it (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md` says how). Then it runs alongside core 0. |

## Time

- Emulated time starts at 0 when the image starts. One instruction of core 0
  takes one cycle; there are 240 000 cycles in an emulated millisecond.
- Everything happens at exact emulated times, and the outputs are
  deterministic (below), but **while core 0 waits, fwtest moves time ahead**,
  so that waiting costs (almost) no instructions and instruction counts
  measure work. The rules for that, and what they do to captures, are
  exact; they follow.

### When fwtest treats core 0 as waiting

Two things, and nothing else, count as waiting:

1. **The wait-for-interrupt instruction**, executed by core 0 while no
   interrupt is pending. Time jumps to one cycle before the next scheduled
   event (below). With nothing scheduled, time doesn't jump.
2. **Polling the free-running timer**: reading its count (HW-13 in
   `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, the 24 MHz time base), outside an interrupt handler
   of core 0, for the third time or more in a row with each read coming
   within 64 cycles (64 instructions of core 0) of the one before. On each
   such read, time jumps ahead by up to 20 µs, and never past one cycle
   before the next scheduled event. The read then returns the count for
   the new time.
   - **Only the spacing of the reads matters.** What the loop does between
     them doesn't: stores to RAM, arithmetic, reads of other registers, a
     call. A loop that reads the count every few instructions *and* writes
     a heartbeat to RAM on every pass is waiting, by this rule.
   - A read more than 64 cycles after the previous one starts the count
     again, so a loop whose reads are at least 64 instructions apart is
     never treated as waiting.
   - Reads made while core 0 is in an interrupt handler are ignored: they
     neither count, nor jump, nor break a sequence.
   - Reads by core 1 count in the same sequence as core 0's: the rule
     looks at reads of the count, not at which core made them.
   - Other timers' counters, their pending flags, and RAM flags are not
     part of this rule. Polling them never moves time ahead.

**Scheduled events** are what the emulated chip and the script have coming
next:
- the end of a timer period;
- an audio half-buffer finishing;
- a transfer completing;
- a MIDI byte arriving;
- an encoder contact changing;
- a script event.

They count whether or not their interrupt is enabled. **Captures, the end
of the run and the watchdog are not scheduled events:** a jump never stops
for them.

### What that does to captures

- fwtest looks at the board between runs of core 0 instructions. Each run
  is at most 1024 instructions, and no longer than the instructions that
  would reach the next capture (or the end of the run) at one cycle each.
  Captures, the watchdog, halts and the end of the run are checked only
  between runs. A capture is taken at the first such stop at or after its
  time.
- **While core 0 is busy (not waiting), captures are exact:** taken at the
  first instruction boundary at or after the time asked.
- **While core 0 waits, a capture can come late**, because every jump
  inside a run moves time without using up the run's instructions:
  - Polling the timer: each read can add up to 20 µs. A loop that reads the
    count every *k* instructions can move up to about 1024 / *k* × 20 µs in
    one run, for example 2 ms when *k* is 10. A capture asked for at *t*
    can be taken that much after *t*.
  - Wait-for-interrupt: each wait jumps to the next scheduled event. A run
    that wakes on every event can cross many of them, for example several
    milliseconds of 100 µs interrupts.
- What is late is the moment the capture is taken, not its label. RAM and
  screen captures show the state at the moment fwtest took them, but are
  named for the time asked (`ram-…-10ms.bin`). `leds.csv`'s `ms` column is
  the time asked, while each duty value covers the real time since the
  previous sample. The end of the run, and so every `end` capture, can come
  late in the same way. `result.json`'s `emulated_ms` says when the run
  really ended.
- The watchdog compares its word between runs, so a hang is noticed up to
  one run late.
- None of this varies between runs: the same image, script and options give
  the same late times, byte for byte, everywhere.

### Getting exact timing

- **Don't wait around the times you capture.** Keep core 0 busy then, for
  example by spacing reads of the timer's count at least 64 instructions
  apart, or by waiting on something else: another timer's pending flag, or
  a RAM flag that an interrupt handler sets. Captures are then exact.
- **Or let the image record the time itself.** Store the timer's count (or
  your own tick count) next to what you capture, and check the capture
  against that stored time instead of the time asked. The M0d firmware's
  beacon does this (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md).
- **For the end of a run**, read `emulated_ms` in `result.json`.
- Instruction counts (`instructions` in `result.json`, `ipb.csv`) do not
  include the time jumped over: a waiting image's counts stay small and
  stable.

### Timers and their acknowledge

The write to a TIMER0 to TIMER3 control register that acknowledges its
interrupt also restarts that timer's count and its period from the moment
of the write. So the time between two of its interrupts is the
period programmed plus the time from the interrupt to the acknowledging
write: about one tick of the 24 MHz time base when the handler acknowledges
first, more when it acknowledges later (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, HW-48). To
measure a period exactly, acknowledge first, or subtract the time the
handler took to reach its acknowledge. Whether the chip does the same is an
open question in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |

WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.

## Input scripts

A text file, one event per line; `#` starts a comment. Times are emulated
milliseconds with up to three decimals. Events at the same time happen in
the order written.

```
# time   event
2        key 12 down
4        key 12 up
6        key 5 tap 3          # down at 6 ms, up at 9 ms (default hold: 50 ms)
10       enc 0 +2             # encoder 0, two detents clockwise
12       enc 3 -1             # one detent anticlockwise
15       pot 300              # the pot now reads 300
20       midi 90 3c 64        # bytes into the MIDI input, in this order
```

| Event | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `key N down`, `key N up` | Key N (0 to 40) pressed or released. |
| `key N tap [HOLD]` | Pressed, then released HOLD ms later (default 50). |
| `enc N +C`, `enc N -C` | Encoder N (0 to 6) turned C detents (1 to 1000); `+` is clockwise. Each detent is four contact changes, 2 ms apart, the first at the event's time. |
| `pot V` | The pot's reading becomes V (0 to 1023). It reads 900 until a script sets it. |
| `midi HH ...` | Bytes (two hex digits each) arrive at the MIDI input one after another, at the wire's pace: one byte every 320 µs, the first 320 µs after the event's time. |

Key, LED and encoder numbers are fwtest's own. `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` maps them
to the panel and to the key matrix.

## Outputs

All in `--out`. A run writes only what it was asked for, plus
`result.json` and `junit.xml`.

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `ram-AAAAAAAA-L-WHEN.bin` | The bytes saved by `--ram` (address as 8 hex digits, length in hex, WHEN as `10ms`, `2.500ms` or `end`). |
| `lcd-WHEN.png` | The screen, 240 x 240, 8-bit RGB, whatever the display's on/off state. Each pixel is the panel's 16-bit colour (5-6-5 bits) with each channel scaled to 8 bits (`c * 255 / 31`, or `/ 63` for green). |
| `leds.csv` | Header `ms,led0,...,led40`, then one row per sample: the sample's time, and for each LED the share of the time since the previous sample (or since the start) that it was lit, in thousandths (0 to 1000, rounded). LED N belongs to key N. |
| `flash.bin` | The flash chip (1 MiB) at the end of the run. |
| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). Core 0's count is exact; core 1's is counted at a granularity of 1024 core-0 instructions. |
| `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |

`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.

- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.

## Outcomes and exit codes

| Exit | Outcome | When |
|------|---------|------|
| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |

When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
means fwtest itself failed.

### Faults and CPU exceptions

fwtest raises no CPU exception: no condition makes interrupt source 0, 1
or 2 pending, so an image's exception handler is never entered by a fault.
What happens instead (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, HW-52, says it with the measured
values):

- Misaligned loads and stores complete. A word load or store uses the 4
  bytes at the address given; a halfword load from an odd RAM address
  ignores the lowest address bit.
- Reads outside every memory and register fwtest models give 0, writes
  there are dropped, and both are listed in `unmodelled_accesses`; so are
  writes to the code window, which are dropped too.
- A division by zero gives 0.
- An instruction fwtest cannot decode ends the run as a fault (exit 3).
  fwtest may stop at the start of the straight-line code that holds it,
  before any of that code has run, and `result.json` then gives that
  address as the fault's `pc`; to have code run up to it, put the
  instruction behind a call or a branch.
- A jump outside every memory runs what fwtest reads there (zeros) for up to
  1024 instructions, until fwtest next checks the program counter, and then
  ends the run as a fault.

## Golden files

`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
without a golden file are not compared.

- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
    within N.
  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
    will use.
- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.

## Suites

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.
