  would reach the next capture (or the end of the run) at one cycle each.
  Captures, the watchdog, halts and the end of the run are checked only
  between runs. A capture is taken at the first such stop at or after its
  time.
- **While core 0 is busy (not waiting), captures are exact:** taken at the
  first instruction boundary at or after the time asked.
- **While core 0 waits, a capture can come late**, because every jump
  inside a run moves time without using up the run's instructions:
  - Polling the timer: each read can add up to 20 µs. A loop that reads the
    count every *k* instructions can move up to about 1024 / *k* × 20 µs in
    one run, for example 2 ms when *k* is 10. A capture asked for at *t*
    can be taken that much after *t*.
  - Wait-for-interrupt: each wait jumps to the next scheduled event. A run
    that wakes on every event can cross many of them, for example several
    milliseconds of 100 µs interrupts.
- What is late is the moment the capture is taken, not its label. RAM and
  screen captures show the state at the moment fwtest took them, but are
  named for the time asked (`ram-…-10ms.bin`). `leds.csv`'s `ms` column is
  the time asked, while each duty value covers the real time since the
  previous sample. The end of the run, and so every `end` capture, can come
  late in the same way. `result.json`'s `emulated_ms` says when the run
  really ended.
- The watchdog compares its word between runs, so a hang is noticed up to
  one run late.
- None of this varies between runs: the same image, script and options give
  the same late times, byte for byte, everywhere.

### Getting exact timing

- **Don't wait around the times you capture.** Keep core 0 busy then, for
  example by spacing reads of the timer's count at least 64 instructions
  apart, or by waiting on something else: another timer's pending flag, or
  a RAM flag that an interrupt handler sets. Captures are then exact.
- **Or let the image record the time itself.** Store the timer's count (or
  your own tick count) next to what you capture, and check the capture
  against that stored time instead of the time asked. The M0d firmware's
  beacon does this (docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md).
- **For the end of a run**, read `emulated_ms` in `result.json`.
- Instruction counts (`instructions` in `result.json`, `ipb.csv`) do not
  include the time jumped over: a waiting image's counts stay small and
  stable.

### Timers and their acknowledge

The write to a TIMER0 to TIMER3 control register that acknowledges its
interrupt also restarts that timer's count and its period from the moment
of the write. So the time between two of its interrupts is the
period programmed plus the time from the interrupt to the acknowledging
write: about one tick of the 24 MHz time base when the handler acknowledges
first, more when it acknowledges later (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, HW-48). To
measure a period exactly, acknowledge first, or subtract the time the
handler took to reach its acknowledge. Whether the chip does the same is an
open question in `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`.

## The command line

```
fwtest run IMAGE --ms MS --out DIR [options]
fwtest suite FILE --out DIR
fwtest version
```

`run` options:

| Option | What it does |
|--------|--------------|
| `--ms MS` | Run for MS emulated milliseconds (up to three decimals). Required. |
| `--out DIR` | Write the outputs here. Required; must be empty or new. |
| `--script FILE` | Timed inputs (below). |
| `--flash FILE` | The flash chip's first bytes (at most 1 MiB); the rest is erased. |
| `--ram ADDR:LEN@WHEN` | Save LEN bytes of memory at ADDR at WHEN. Numbers in decimal, or hex with `0x`. Only RAM (main RAM and the other RAM banks `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` lists) can be saved; anything else is a usage error. Repeatable. |
| `--lcd WHEN` | Save the screen as a PNG at WHEN. Repeatable. |
| `--leds-every MS` | Sample the LEDs every MS into `leds.csv`. |
| `--flash-out` | Save the whole flash chip at the end (`flash.bin`). |
| `--wav` | Save the audio output (`audio.wav`). |
| `--ipb` | Save instructions per audio block (`ipb.csv`). |
| `--console` | Save the bytes written to the chip's debug message register (`console.txt`; `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` names it). |
| `--watchdog ADDR:MS` | A hang if the 32-bit word at RAM address ADDR stays the same for more than MS ms. |
| `--halt-ok` | A halt counts as success (exit 0). |
| `--golden DIR` | Compare the outputs with the golden files in DIR (below). |

WHEN is a time in ms (`10`, `2.5`) or `end`. The run ends at `--ms`, or
earlier on a fault, halt or hang; `end` captures are taken then.

## Input scripts

A text file, one event per line; `#` starts a comment. Times are emulated
milliseconds with up to three decimals. Events at the same time happen in
the order written.

```
# time   event
2        key 12 down
4        key 12 up
6        key 5 tap 3          # down at 6 ms, up at 9 ms (default hold: 50 ms)
10       enc 0 +2             # encoder 0, two detents clockwise
12       enc 3 -1             # one detent anticlockwise
15       pot 300              # the pot now reads 300
20       midi 90 3c 64        # bytes into the MIDI input, in this order
```

| Event | Meaning |
|-------|---------|
| `key N down`, `key N up` | Key N (0 to 40) pressed or released. |
| `key N tap [HOLD]` | Pressed, then released HOLD ms later (default 50). |
| `enc N +C`, `enc N -C` | Encoder N (0 to 6) turned C detents (1 to 1000); `+` is clockwise. Each detent is four contact changes, 2 ms apart, the first at the event's time. |
| `pot V` | The pot's reading becomes V (0 to 1023). It reads 900 until a script sets it. |
| `midi HH ...` | Bytes (two hex digits each) arrive at the MIDI input one after another, at the wire's pace: one byte every 320 µs, the first 320 µs after the event's time. |

Key, LED and encoder numbers are fwtest's own. `HARDWARE-SPEC.md` maps them
to the panel and to the key matrix.

## Outputs

All in `--out`. A run writes only what it was asked for, plus
`result.json` and `junit.xml`.

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `ram-AAAAAAAA-L-WHEN.bin` | The bytes saved by `--ram` (address as 8 hex digits, length in hex, WHEN as `10ms`, `2.500ms` or `end`). |
| `lcd-WHEN.png` | The screen, 240 x 240, 8-bit RGB, whatever the display's on/off state. Each pixel is the panel's 16-bit colour (5-6-5 bits) with each channel scaled to 8 bits (`c * 255 / 31`, or `/ 63` for green). |
| `leds.csv` | Header `ms,led0,...,led40`, then one row per sample: the sample's time, and for each LED the share of the time since the previous sample (or since the start) that it was lit, in thousandths (0 to 1000, rounded). LED N belongs to key N. |
| `flash.bin` | The flash chip (1 MiB) at the end of the run. |
| `audio.wav` | The audio output: 16-bit PCM, stereo, the header says 44 100 Hz. Every sample the output played, in order. How the firmware feeds the output, and its exact rate: `HARDWARE-SPEC.md`. |
| `ipb.csv` | Header `block,end_ms,core0,core1`, then one row per audio block (each time the output finished one half of its buffer): its number, the time it finished, and the instructions core 0 and core 1 executed since the previous block (the first row: since the start). Core 0's count is exact; core 1's is counted at a granularity of 1024 core-0 instructions. |
| `console.txt` | The debug console bytes, as written. |
| `result.json` | What happened (below). |
| `junit.xml` | JUnit XML: a test case `run` (fails on a fault or hang, and on a halt without `--halt-ok`), and one `golden NAME` per golden file. |

`result.json` holds: `fwtest` (version and the emulator build it carries),
`image` (file name, size, SHA-256), `script_sha256`, `run` (`outcome`,
`detail`, `emulated_ms`, `instructions` per core, `midi_bytes_dropped`,
`unmodelled_accesses`, and every output's name, size and SHA-256), `golden`
(each file's `match` or `mismatch` and why), and `exit_code`.

- `midi_bytes_dropped`: bytes that arrived while the image had no MIDI
  receiver set up, or more than about a second's worth waiting.
- `unmodelled_accesses`: addresses the image read or wrote that fwtest does
  not model (reads give 0, writes are dropped), with counts, up to 256.
  Usually a sign the image touched something unexpected; if the hardware
  has something there, ask for it in a spec request.

## Outcomes and exit codes

| Exit | Outcome | When |
|------|---------|------|
| 0 | completed | Ran for `--ms`, and every golden file matched. (Also a halt with `--halt-ok`.) |
| 1 | golden mismatch | A golden file differs (beyond its tolerance), or an output it names is missing. |
| 2 | usage error | Bad arguments, an unreadable or oversized image, a bad script, `--out` not empty, a capture outside RAM. Nothing ran. |
| 3 | fault | A core met an instruction it cannot decode or the emulator does not implement, or its program counter left every memory that can hold code (the image, RAM, the other RAM banks). |
| 4 | halt | Core 0 executed a jump to itself with interrupts disabled: a deliberate stop. The run ends there. |
| 5 | hang | The `--watchdog` word did not change for longer than its time. |

When several apply, the first in this order wins: 2, 3, 5, 1, 4, 0. Captures
and `result.json` are written for 1, 3, 4 and 5 too. Any other exit code
means fwtest itself failed.

### Faults and CPU exceptions

fwtest raises no CPU exception: no condition makes interrupt source 0, 1
or 2 pending, so an image's exception handler is never entered by a fault.
What happens instead (`HARDWARE-SPEC.md`, HW-52, says it with the measured
values):

- Misaligned loads and stores complete. A word load or store uses the 4
  bytes at the address given; a halfword load from an odd RAM address
  ignores the lowest address bit.
- Reads outside every memory and register fwtest models give 0, writes
  there are dropped, and both are listed in `unmodelled_accesses`; so are
  writes to the code window, which are dropped too.
- A division by zero gives 0.
- An instruction fwtest cannot decode ends the run as a fault (exit 3).
  fwtest may stop at the start of the straight-line code that holds it,
  before any of that code has run, and `result.json` then gives that
  address as the fault's `pc`; to have code run up to it, put the
  instruction behind a call or a branch.
- A jump outside every memory runs what fwtest reads there (zeros) for up to
  1024 instructions, until fwtest next checks the program counter, and then
  ends the run as a fault.

## Golden files

`--golden DIR`: every file in DIR is a golden file, compared with the output
of the same name. A golden file without such an output is a mismatch. Outputs
without a golden file are not compared.

- **Exact by default:** byte for byte. Every fwtest output is deterministic,
  so exact is right unless the firmware's own behaviour is meant to vary.
- **Tolerances**, where an output is meant to be approximate: a text file
  `NAME.tolerance` beside the golden file, one line:
  - `pixel-diff N` (a `.png`): same size; each colour channel of each pixel
    within N.
  - `sample-diff N` (a `.wav`): same format and length; each sample within N.
  - `rel-percent P` (a `.csv`): same lines and fields; text fields equal;
    each integer within P percent of the golden value (at least 1). For
    example `ipb.csv` with `rel-percent 3` is the performance gate R-PERF-2
    will use.
- Golden PNG and WAV files compared with a tolerance must be ones fwtest
  wrote. To make a golden file, run once, check the output by hand, and copy
  it into the golden folder in the same commit as the test.

## Suites

`fwtest suite FILE --out DIR` runs several cases. Each line of FILE:

```
# NAME  EXPECT     IMAGE                 run options (paths relative to FILE)
boot    completed  ../out/build/app.bin  --ms 50 --ram 0x01c00000:16@end --golden golden/boot
stop    halt       images/stop.bin       --ms 10
```

NAME (letters, digits, `-`, `_`) is the case's output folder under DIR.
EXPECT is the outcome expected: `completed`, `halt`, `fault` or `hang`. A
case passes when its outcome is EXPECT and every golden file matches. DIR
also gets `result.json` (every case's result) and `junit.xml` (one test case
per suite case). The exit code is 0 when every case passes, 1 otherwise, 2
on a usage error.

## Determinism

The same image, script, options and fwtest build give byte-identical outputs
on every run and every machine: no host time, no randomness that isn't
seeded the same way every run, nothing from the environment, no host paths
in the results. CI runs the harness's own suite twice in fresh containers
and compares every output byte (C-HARNESS-DET). If two runs of yours ever
differ, that is a bug in fwtest: report it.

## Versions

`fwtest version` prints fwtest's version and the emulator build it carries;
`result.json` has both. The image is identified by its digest. When the
harness changes, a pull request moves `config/fwtest-image` to the new
digest, so a firmware test always names the exact runner it used.

<!--
SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98

# Requirements

Numbered requirements for this project (the original, MIT-licensed base
firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, JieLi AC791N). Every check names the
requirements it covers (`tools/record.py`, `CHECKS`), and every test record
ends with a traceability table: requirement → checks → result.

A requirement whose "Checked by" says *review* is checked by people when they
review a pull request, not by a machine. *Planned* means a later milestone
adds the check. The record lists both kinds, so nothing looks checked when it
isn't.

The four founding requirements (docs/prompts/M0a.md): **history**,
**tests**, **reproducible**, **public and efficient**.

| ID | Requirement | Since | Checked by |
|----|-------------|-------|------------|
| R-PROC-1 | Every commit message follows `.gitmessage` (subject `<area>: <summary>`; non-empty What, Why, How, Result, Sources, Exposure). Agent-written commits also carry `Model:` and `Claude-Session:` trailers. Merge commits are exempt; their pull request carries the sections. | M0a | C-COMMIT-MSG, C-UNIT |
| R-PROC-2 | main changes only through pull requests that passed CI, merged by the owner with a verified, signed merge commit (GitHub's merge button since 2026-10-22, CONTRIBUTING.md "Merge policy"). Nobody bypasses. No force pushes or deletion on main and `records`; `m*` tags are never moved or deleted. | M0a | rulesets (CONTRIBUTING.md); C-MERGE (records workflow) |
| R-PROC-3 | Each milestone's prompt is committed unedited in `docs/prompts/` in the commit that starts the milestone. | M0a | review |
| R-PROC-4 | Every check names the requirements it checks, and every record has a traceability table. | M0a | C-UNIT |
| R-REC-1 | Each commit pushed to main gets a permanent record `records/<sha>/` (report.json, report.md, logs) on the orphan `records` branch, written only by the records workflow, never for pull requests. A record is never changed: a later re-check of C-MERGE alone, started by hand with the merge check on main (`.github/workflows/recheck-merge.yml`), only adds `records/<sha>/verified-<date>/` beside it, naming the checker's commit and why. | M0a | records.yml; C-UNIT (record writer) |

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 japes98
"""Runs the firmware's fwtest suite and checks what it captured (check
C-FW-SUITE; R-BOOT-1 to R-BOOT-5, R-CLK-1, R-IRQ-1 to R-IRQ-4, R-LCD-1
to R-LCD-5).

  fw-suite.py --build DIR --out DIR

Copies DIR/app.bin (a tools/build.sh output) to out/fw/app.bin and builds
the test images (TEST_BUILDS: the same source with one SB_TEST_* define
each) to out/fw/<name>.bin, where tests/fw/boot.suite expects them, runs
the suite through tools/fwtest (the pinned image), and then checks:

- every case: the outcome the suite expects, no unmodelled accesses, core
  1 never ran;
- boot: the marker; the vector table, every slot (HW-18): source 4 is
  sb_tick, every other source its own stub in crt0.S, by the ELF's
  symbols; the clock measured at startup: SB_CLOCK_CYCLES core cycles take
  CLOCK_TICKS time base ticks (240 MHz against 24 MHz, HW-11, HW-13); the
  first tick within FIRST_TICK_MS of the start (from the last tick's time
  base, the ticks taken and the shortest interval, since the run itself
  ends late); nothing halted;
- heartbeat (one emulated second; the image idles between ticks, so
  captures come late, docs/HARNESS.md "Time"): at every capture at least
  one of the beacon's two heartbeat copies is consistent, beats ==
  ticks // 24000, and both are when its seq is even (the tick handler
  writes them in turn, DESIGN-NOTES.md M1); the consistent copy's ticks
  are no earlier than the time asked less one tick period and START_SLACK,
  and no more than LATE_MS after it; beats never go back. At the end:
  the last tick's time base lies within one tick period (and START_SLACK)
  before fwtest's emulated end time; every interval between two ticks is
  within INTERVAL_TOL of 24 000 time base ticks (1 ms), and so is their
  spread (jitter); beats and ticks taken differ by at most one; the idle
  wait returned once per tick, and core 0 ran at most IDLE_MAX_IPT
  instructions per tick (M0's polling heartbeat: M0_IPP per period);
- fault and stray: the halt recorded in the beacon (reason and source),
  and the console line, by golden file;
- badinsn: fwtest's own fault outcome for an undecodable instruction. A
  limit of the harness, not firmware behaviour: no handler of ours runs
  (SR-1).
- heartbeat2 (since M2): the heartbeat's checks again over 2.25 s; with
  heartbeat (1.25 s) its difference is the steady state, which may take
  at most IDLE_MAX_IPT instructions a tick. The idle loop's wakes, stored
  once a second, equal the ticks taken since it began, within one.
- screen (since M2): every pixel of the address pattern (300 ms) against
  its formula; the test screen's border, corners and ramps pixel by pixel
  (800 ms); one heartbeat later (1 500 ms) only the heartbeat's rows
  changed; the beacon's screen and seconds shown at each capture; and the
  three pictures against golden images.
- flood (since M2): a test build that sends whole frames back to back from
  500 ms: every tick interval still within INTERVAL_TOL, far more frames
  than ticks, and the picture still the test screen. Prints how long a
  whole frame takes.

Prints what it saw for the record, and exits 1 if anything failed.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import struct
import subprocess
import sys
import zlib

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SUITE = "tests/fw/boot.suite"
IMAGE = os.path.join("out", "fw", "app.bin")
# Test images: name -> define (firmware/src/probe.c).
TEST_BUILDS = {"test-fault": "SB_TEST_FAULT", "test-stray": "SB_TEST_STRAY",
               "test-badinsn": "SB_TEST_BADINSN", "test-flood": "SB_TEST_FLOOD"}
# Each case's expected outcome (the suite says the same; checked twice).
EXPECT = {"boot": "completed", "heartbeat": "completed", "heartbeat2": "completed",
          "screen": "completed", "flood": "completed", "fault": "halt", "stray": "halt",
          "badinsn": "fault"}

MARKER = 0x44304253        # "SB0D", firmware/src/sb.h
TICKS_PER_MS = 24000       # HW-13
START_SLACK = 240          # ticks: 10 microseconds (main starts the time base)
# Startup clears .bss before main starts the time base, at most this many
# core cycles a word (2 measured in M2), 10 cycles a time base tick: since
# M2's frame buffer that is about a quarter of a millisecond, so the slack
# grows with the image's bss (start_slack).
CLEAR_CYCLES_PER_WORD = 3
LATE_MS = 30               # a waiting core 0 crosses many ticks in one run
INTERVAL_TOL = 24          # ticks: 1 microsecond, 0.1% of a tick period
CLOCK_TICKS = (240, 241)   # SB_CLOCK_CYCLES = 2402 cycles at 10 a tick
FIRST_TICK_MS = 2          # the first tick: one period after main starts it
IDLE_MAX_IPT = 100         # instructions per tick, in steady state (since M2)
M0_IPP = 356.887           # M0's instructions per period (its last record)
STUB_SIZE = 2              # crt0.S's sb_irq_stubs
SRC_TICK = 4               # TIMER0 (HW-16, HW-19)
SRC_SPI1 = 16              # SPI1, the panel's transfers (HW-29)
HALT_STRAY, HALT_FAULT, HALT_STACK = 1, 2, 3

BEACON_FIELDS = ("marker", "beats", "ticks", "period", "seq", "beats_b", "ticks_b",
                 "tick_count", "interval_min", "interval_max", "wakes", "clock",
                 "halt_reason", "halt_source", "halt_reti",
                 # since M2 (firmware/src/sb.h)
                 "screen", "loop_ticks", "frames", "frame_ticks", "render_ticks", "beat_ticks",
                 "shown", "chunks", "wakes_ticks")
BEACON_LEN = 4 * len(BEACON_FIELDS)
CAPTURE = re.compile(r"^ram-01c00000-%x-(?P<when>[0-9.]+ms|end)\.bin$" % BEACON_LEN)
VECTORS = "ram-01c7fe00-200-end.bin"


def beacon(data):
    return dict(zip(BEACON_FIELDS, struct.unpack("<%dI" % len(BEACON_FIELDS), data)))


def elf_symbols(path):
    """name -> value, from an ELF32 little-endian file's symbol table."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        elf = f.read()
    shoff, = struct.unpack_from("<I", elf, 0x20)
    shentsize, shnum = struct.unpack_from("<HH", elf, 0x2E)
    sections = [struct.unpack_from("<IIIIIIIIII", elf, shoff + i * shentsize) for i in range(shnum)]
    syms = {}
    for s in sections:
        if s[1] != 2:      # SHT_SYMTAB
            continue
        strtab = sections[s[6]]
        for off in range(s[4], s[4] + s[5], 16):
            name, value = struct.unpack_from("<II", elf, off)
            end = elf.index(b"\0", strtab[4] + name)
            syms[elf[strtab[4] + name:end].decode()] = value
    return syms


def check_case(name, result):
    """Problems with one case's result.json."""
    run = result.get("run", {})
    problems = []
    if run.get("outcome") != EXPECT[name]:
        problems.append("%s: outcome %s, not %s (%s)" % (name, run.get("outcome"), EXPECT[name],
                                                         run.get("detail")))
    if run.get("unmodelled_accesses"):
        problems.append("%s: unmodelled accesses %s" % (name, run["unmodelled_accesses"]))
    if run.get("instructions", {}).get("core1", 0) != 0:
        problems.append("%s: core 1 ran" % name)
    return problems


def consistent(b):
    """The heartbeat copies that are consistent: [(beats, ticks), ...]."""
    return [(be, ti) for be, ti in ((b["beats"], b["ticks"]), (b["beats_b"], b["ticks_b"]))
            if be == ti // TICKS_PER_MS]


def start_slack(bss):
    """Time base ticks by which main may start the time base after fwtest's
    emulated time began: START_SLACK and the clearing of bss."""
    return START_SLACK + (bss // 4 * CLEAR_CYCLES_PER_WORD + 9) // 10


def check_beacon(when_ms, b, end_ms=None):
    """Problems with one beacon captured at when_ms (the time asked; end_ms
    is result.json's emulated_ms for the capture at the end)."""
    problems = []
    if b["marker"] != MARKER:
        problems.append("marker 0x%08x, not 0x%08x" % (b["marker"], MARKER))
    if b["period"] != TICKS_PER_MS:
        problems.append("period %d, not %d" % (b["period"], TICKS_PER_MS))
        return problems
    good = consistent(b)
    if not good:
        return problems + ["neither heartbeat copy is consistent: %d beats after %d ticks, %d after %d"
                           % (b["beats"], b["ticks"], b["beats_b"], b["ticks_b"])]
    if b["seq"] % 2 == 0 and (len(good) != 2 or good[0] != good[1]):
        problems.append("seq %d is even, but the two heartbeat copies differ" % b["seq"])
    ticks = good[-1][1]
    if end_ms is not None:
        end = round(end_ms * TICKS_PER_MS)
        if not -START_SLACK <= end - ticks <= TICKS_PER_MS + INTERVAL_TOL + START_SLACK:
            problems.append("last tick at %d ticks, not within one tick period before the end (%d)"
                            % (ticks, end))
    else:
        low = round((when_ms - 1) * TICKS_PER_MS) - INTERVAL_TOL - START_SLACK
        high = round((when_ms + LATE_MS) * TICKS_PER_MS)
        if not low <= ticks <= high:
            problems.append("%d ticks at %s ms, not within %d to %d" % (ticks, when_ms, low, high))
    return problems


def check_ticks(b, result):
    """Problems with the end beacon's tick statistics, and lines to print."""
    problems = []
    n, lo, hi = b["tick_count"], b["interval_min"], b["interval_max"]
    loop = b["wakes_ticks"] - b["loop_ticks"]
    lines = ["  ticks %d, interval %d to %d time base ticks (jitter %d); the idle loop's wait returned"
             " %d times in its first %d ticks" % (n, lo, hi, hi - lo, b["wakes"], loop)]
    if n < 2:
        return ["heartbeat: %d ticks" % n], lines
    for name, v in (("shortest", lo), ("longest", hi)):
        if abs(v - TICKS_PER_MS) > INTERVAL_TOL:
            problems.append("heartbeat: %s tick interval %d, not within %d of %d"
                            % (name, v, INTERVAL_TOL, TICKS_PER_MS))

    """Steady-state instructions per tick, from the two heartbeat cases
    (the same options but their length: R-IRQ-1 since M2), and lines."""

             " (M0's polling heartbeat: %.1f a period)" % (i2 - i1, dn, ipt, M0_IPP)]
    if ipt > IDLE_MAX_IPT:
        return ["heartbeat: %.1f instructions a tick in steady state, more than %d" % (ipt, IDLE_MAX_IPT)], lines
    return [], lines

    """Problems with the heartbeat case's captures, and lines to print."""
    end_ms = float(result["run"]["emulated_ms"])
    caps = []
    for n in os.listdir(case_dir):
        m = CAPTURE.match(n)
        if m:
            when = m.group("when")
            caps.append((end_ms if when == "end" else float(when[:-2]), when, n))
    caps.sort()
    problems, lines, last, end = [], [], -1, None
    if len(caps) < 2:
        problems.append("heartbeat: %d beacon captures, expected several" % len(caps))
    for when_ms, when, n in caps:
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, n), "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        if len(data) != BEACON_LEN:
            problems.append("%s: %d bytes" % (n, len(data)))
            continue
        b = beacon(data)
        lines.append("  %-6s seq %5d  beats %5d  ticks %9d (%.3f ms)  copy b %5d %9d"

            end = b

    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, VECTORS), "rb") as f:

    want = [symbols["sb_irq_stubs"] + STUB_SIZE * n for n in range(128)]

def read_png(path):
    """(width, height, rows of (r, g, b)) from an 8-bit RGB, non-interlaced
    PNG, as fwtest writes them (docs/HARNESS.md, lcd-WHEN.png)."""
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    if data[:8] != b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n":
        raise ValueError("not a PNG")
    pos, idat, w = 8, b"", None
    while pos < len(data):
        n, kind = struct.unpack_from(">I4s", data, pos)
        body = data[pos + 8:pos + 8 + n]
        if kind == b"IHDR":
            w, h, depth, ctype, _, _, interlace = struct.unpack(">IIBBBBB", body)
            if (depth, ctype, interlace) != (8, 2, 0):
                raise ValueError("not 8-bit RGB without interlace")
        elif kind == b"IDAT":
            idat += body
        pos += 12 + n
    raw, stride, rows, prev = zlib.decompress(idat), w * 3, [], bytearray(w * 3)
    for y in range(h):
        kind, line = raw[y * (stride + 1)], bytearray(raw[y * (stride + 1) + 1:(y + 1) * (stride + 1)])
        for i in range(stride):
            a = line[i - 3] if i >= 3 else 0
            b, c = prev[i], prev[i - 3] if i >= 3 else 0
            if kind == 1:
                line[i] = (line[i] + a) & 255
            elif kind == 2:
                line[i] = (line[i] + b) & 255
            elif kind == 3:
                line[i] = (line[i] + (a + b) // 2) & 255
            elif kind == 4:
                p = a + b - c
                pa, pb, pc = abs(p - a), abs(p - b), abs(p - c)
                line[i] = (line[i] + (a if pa <= pb and pa <= pc else b if pb <= pc else c)) & 255
        rows.append([tuple(line[i:i + 3]) for i in range(0, stride, 3)])
        prev = line
    return w, h, rows


def rgb8(r5, g6, b5):
    """The colour fwtest's PNG shows for an RGB565 pixel."""
    return (r5 * 255 // 31, g6 * 255 // 63, b5 * 255 // 31)

WHITE, RED, GREEN, BLUE, YELLOW = (rgb8(31, 63, 31), rgb8(31, 0, 0), rgb8(0, 63, 0),
                                   rgb8(0, 0, 31), rgb8(31, 63, 0))
CORNERS = (((3, 3), RED), ((225, 3), GREEN), ((3, 225), BLUE), ((225, 225), YELLOW))
BEAT_ROWS = range(200, 216)


def check_pattern(rows):
    """Problems with the address pattern: every pixel's colour must say
    where it is (screen.c's screen_pattern), so the orientation, the
    colour order and every pixel's address are checked at once."""
    bad = [(x, y) for y in range(240) for x in range(240)
           if rows[y][x] != rgb8(x >> 3, y >> 2, (x & 7) << 2 | (y & 3))]
    if bad:
        return ["screen: %d pixels of the address pattern are wrong, the first at %s" % (len(bad), bad[0])]
    return []


def check_test_screen(rows):
    """Problems with the test screen's fixed parts: the border, the corner
    squares and the three ramps (screen.c's screen_test)."""
    problems = []
    edge = [(x, y) for y in range(240) for x in range(240)
            if (x in (0, 239) or y in (0, 239)) and rows[y][x] != WHITE]
    if edge:
        problems.append("screen: %d edge pixels are not white, the first at %s" % (len(edge), edge[0]))
    for (x0, y0), colour in CORNERS:
        wrong = [(x, y) for y in range(y0, y0 + 12) for x in range(x0, x0 + 12) if rows[y][x] != colour]
        if wrong:
            problems.append("screen: the corner square at %s is not %s (first wrong pixel %s: %s)"
                            % ((x0, y0), colour, wrong[0], rows[wrong[0][1]][wrong[0][0]]))
    for name, y0, steps, width, colour in (("red", 44, 32, 6, lambda i: rgb8(i, 0, 0)),
                                           ("green", 60, 64, 3, lambda i: rgb8(0, i, 0)),
                                           ("blue", 76, 32, 6, lambda i: rgb8(0, 0, i))):
        wrong = [(x, y) for i in range(steps) for x in range(24 + width * i, 24 + width * (i + 1))
                 for y in range(y0, y0 + 14) if rows[y][x] != colour(i)]
        if wrong:
            problems.append("screen: the %s ramp is wrong at %s" % (name, wrong[0]))
    return problems


def check_screen(case_dir):
    """Problems with the screen case: the address pattern at 300 ms, the
    test screen at 800 ms and 1 500 ms (the heartbeat one second on, and
    nothing else changed), and the beacon captured with each; lines."""
    problems, lines, shots, beacons = [], [], {}, {}
    for when in (300, 800, 1500):
        try:
            w, h, shots[when] = read_png(os.path.join(case_dir, "lcd-%dms.png" % when))
        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
            return ["screen: lcd-%dms.png: %s" % (when, e)], lines
        if (w, h) != (240, 240):
            problems.append("screen: lcd-%dms.png is %dx%d" % (when, w, h))
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-%dms.bin" % (BEACON_LEN, when)), "rb") as f:
            beacons[when] = beacon(f.read())
    if problems:
        return problems, lines
    problems += check_pattern(shots[300])
    problems += check_test_screen(shots[800])
    changed = {y for y in range(240) for x in range(240) if shots[800][y][x] != shots[1500][y][x]}
    if not changed or not changed <= set(BEAT_ROWS):
        problems.append("screen: from 800 to 1 500 ms rows %s changed, not some of the heartbeat's %d to %d only"
                        % (sorted(changed)[:8], BEAT_ROWS[0], BEAT_ROWS[-1]))
    for when, (screen, shown) in ((300, (1, None)), (800, (2, 0)), (1500, (2, 1))):
        b = beacons[when]
        good = consistent(b)
        seconds = good[-1][0] // 1000 if good else None
        lines.append("  %4d ms: screen %d, heartbeat shown %d s, beats %s" % (when, b["screen"], b["shown"],
                                                                            good[-1][0] if good else "?"))
        if b["screen"] != screen:
            problems.append("screen %d ms: the beacon says screen %d, not %d" % (when, b["screen"], screen))
        if shown is not None and (b["shown"] != shown or seconds != shown):
            problems.append("screen %d ms: heartbeat shown %d at %s whole seconds, expected %d"
                            % (when, b["shown"], seconds, shown))
    return problems, lines


def check_flood(case_dir, result, screen_dir):
    """Problems with the flood case (whole frames back to back): every tick
    interval still within INTERVAL_TOL, frames going out, and the picture
    still the test screen; lines with the frame time."""
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
        b = beacon(f.read())
    problems, lines = [], []
    n, lo, hi = b["tick_count"], b["interval_min"], b["interval_max"]
    ms = float(result["run"]["emulated_ms"])
    instr = result["run"]["instructions"]["core0"]
    flood = b["frames"] - 2       # the two frames before the flood
    lines.append("  ticks %d, interval %d to %d time base ticks (jitter %d), during %d whole frames"
                 % (n, lo, hi, hi - lo, flood))
    if flood > 0:
        lines.append("  a whole frame: %d time base ticks (%.2f us) from its window to its last transfer"
                     " started; %.0f core-0 instructions a frame over the run"
                     % (b["frame_ticks"], b["frame_ticks"] / 24.0, instr / b["frames"]))
    for name, v in (("shortest", lo), ("longest", hi)):
        if abs(v - TICKS_PER_MS) > INTERVAL_TOL:
            problems.append("flood: %s tick interval %d, not within %d of %d" % (name, v, INTERVAL_TOL, TICKS_PER_MS))
    # The flood starts with the test screen, at 500 ms; a frame is a few
    # microseconds of the core's time in fwtest, so far more frames than
    # ticks go out.
    if n < ms - 2 or flood < 10 * (n - 500):
        problems.append("flood: %d ticks and %d frames in %.3f ms, expected a tick a ms and more than ten"
                        " frames a tick after 500 ms" % (n, flood, ms))
    try:
        _, _, end = read_png(os.path.join(case_dir, "lcd-end.png"))
        _, _, ref = read_png(os.path.join(screen_dir, "lcd-800ms.png"))
        if end != ref:
            problems.append("flood: the picture at the end is not the test screen")
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        problems.append("flood: %s" % e)
    return problems, lines


def build_tests(build):
    """Builds the test images; returns problems."""
    problems = []
    for name, define in sorted(TEST_BUILDS.items()):
        out = os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", "build-" + name)
        p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", out, "--define", define],
                           cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            problems.append("%s: the build failed:\n%s" % (name, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-2000:]))
            continue
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(out, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", name + ".bin"))
        print("built %s (-D%s)" % (name, define))
    return problems


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    global START_SLACK
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            sizes = dict(l.split() for l in f if l.strip())
        print("image size: " + ", ".join("%s %s" % kv for kv in sizes.items()))
        START_SLACK = start_slack(int(sizes.get("bss", 0)))
        print("start slack: %d time base ticks (bss cleared before main starts the time base)" % START_SLACK)
    symbols = elf_symbols(os.path.join(a.build, "app.elf"))
    problems = build_tests(a.build)

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    if p.returncode != 0:
        problems.append("fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode)

    steady = {}
    for name in EXPECT:
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        for g in result.get("golden") or []:
            print("  golden %s: %s" % (g.get("name"), g.get("result")))
            if g.get("result") != "match":
                problems.append("%s: golden %s: %s" % (name, g.get("name"), g.get("detail")))
        if name in ("boot", "screen", "fault", "stray") and not result.get("golden"):
            problems.append("%s: no golden files compared" % name)
        case_dir = os.path.join(out, name)
        more, lines = [], []
        if name == "boot":
            more, lines = check_boot(case_dir, symbols)
        elif name in ("heartbeat", "heartbeat2") and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(case_dir, result)
            with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
                steady[name] = (result, beacon(f.read()))
            if len(steady) == 2:
                m, l = check_steady([steady["heartbeat"][0], steady["heartbeat2"][0]],
                                    [steady["heartbeat"][1], steady["heartbeat2"][1]])
                more, lines = more + m, lines + l
        elif name == "screen":
            more, lines = check_screen(case_dir)
        elif name == "flood" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_flood(case_dir, result, os.path.join(out, "screen"))
        elif name == "fault":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STACK, 1)
        elif name == "stray":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STRAY, 127)
        problems += more
        if lines:
            print("\n".join(lines))

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0

def check_steady(results, ends):
    """Steady-state instructions per tick, from the two heartbeat cases
    (the same options but their length: R-IRQ-1 since M2), and lines."""
    (r1, r2), (b1, b2) = results, ends
    i1, i2 = r1["run"]["instructions"]["core0"], r2["run"]["instructions"]["core0"]
    dn = b2["tick_count"] - b1["tick_count"]
    if dn <= 0:
        return ["heartbeat2: no more ticks than heartbeat"], []
    ipt = (i2 - i1) / dn
    lines = ["  steady state: %d instructions for %d ticks between the two heartbeat runs: %.3f a tick"
             " (M0's polling heartbeat: %.1f a period)" % (i2 - i1, dn, ipt, M0_IPP)]
    if ipt > IDLE_MAX_IPT:
        return ["heartbeat: %.1f instructions a tick in steady state, more than %d" % (ipt, IDLE_MAX_IPT)], lines
    return [], lines


def check_heartbeat(case_dir, result):
    """Problems with the heartbeat case's captures, and lines to print."""
    end_ms = float(result["run"]["emulated_ms"])
    caps = []
    for n in os.listdir(case_dir):
        m = CAPTURE.match(n)
        if m:
            when = m.group("when")
            caps.append((end_ms if when == "end" else float(when[:-2]), when, n))
    caps.sort()
    problems, lines, last, end = [], [], -1, None
    if len(caps) < 2:
        problems.append("heartbeat: %d beacon captures, expected several" % len(caps))
    for when_ms, when, n in caps:
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, n), "rb") as f:
            data = f.read()
        if len(data) != BEACON_LEN:
            problems.append("%s: %d bytes" % (n, len(data)))
            continue
        b = beacon(data)
        lines.append("  %-6s seq %5d  beats %5d  ticks %9d (%.3f ms)  copy b %5d %9d"
                     % (when, b["seq"], b["beats"], b["ticks"], b["ticks"] / TICKS_PER_MS,
                        b["beats_b"], b["ticks_b"]))
        problems += ["heartbeat %s: %s" % (when, p) for p in
                     check_beacon(when_ms, b, end_ms if when == "end" else None)]
        good = consistent(b)
        if good and good[-1][0] < last:
            problems.append("heartbeat %s: beats went back from %d to %d" % (when, last, good[-1][0]))
        last = good[-1][0] if good else last
        if when == "end":
            end = b
    if end is not None:
        more, tick_lines = check_ticks(end, result)
        problems += more
        lines += tick_lines
    return problems, lines

CORNERS = (((3, 3), RED), ((225, 3), GREEN), ((3, 225), BLUE), ((225, 225), YELLOW))
BEAT_ROWS = range(200, 216)


def check_pattern(rows):
    """Problems with the address pattern: every pixel's colour must say
    where it is (screen.c's screen_pattern), so the orientation, the
    colour order and every pixel's address are checked at once."""
    bad = [(x, y) for y in range(240) for x in range(240)
           if rows[y][x] != rgb8(x >> 3, y >> 2, (x & 7) << 2 | (y & 3))]
    if bad:
        return ["screen: %d pixels of the address pattern are wrong, the first at %s" % (len(bad), bad[0])]
    return []


def check_test_screen(rows):
    """Problems with the test screen's fixed parts: the border, the corner
    squares and the three ramps (screen.c's screen_test)."""
    problems = []
    edge = [(x, y) for y in range(240) for x in range(240)
            if (x in (0, 239) or y in (0, 239)) and rows[y][x] != WHITE]
    if edge:
        problems.append("screen: %d edge pixels are not white, the first at %s" % (len(edge), edge[0]))
    for (x0, y0), colour in CORNERS:
        wrong = [(x, y) for y in range(y0, y0 + 12) for x in range(x0, x0 + 12) if rows[y][x] != colour]
        if wrong:
            problems.append("screen: the corner square at %s is not %s (first wrong pixel %s: %s)"
                            % ((x0, y0), colour, wrong[0], rows[wrong[0][1]][wrong[0][0]]))
    for name, y0, steps, width, colour in (("red", 44, 32, 6, lambda i: rgb8(i, 0, 0)),
                                           ("green", 60, 64, 3, lambda i: rgb8(0, i, 0)),
                                           ("blue", 76, 32, 6, lambda i: rgb8(0, 0, i))):
        wrong = [(x, y) for i in range(steps) for x in range(24 + width * i, 24 + width * (i + 1))
                 for y in range(y0, y0 + 14) if rows[y][x] != colour(i)]
        if wrong:
            problems.append("screen: the %s ramp is wrong at %s" % (name, wrong[0]))
    return problems


def check_screen(case_dir):
    """Problems with the screen case: the address pattern at 300 ms, the
    test screen at 800 ms and 1 500 ms (the heartbeat one second on, and
    nothing else changed), and the beacon captured with each; lines."""
    problems, lines, shots, beacons = [], [], {}, {}
    for when in (300, 800, 1500):
        try:
            w, h, shots[when] = read_png(os.path.join(case_dir, "lcd-%dms.png" % when))
        except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
            return ["screen: lcd-%dms.png: %s" % (when, e)], lines
        if (w, h) != (240, 240):
            problems.append("screen: lcd-%dms.png is %dx%d" % (when, w, h))
        with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-%dms.bin" % (BEACON_LEN, when)), "rb") as f:
            beacons[when] = beacon(f.read())
    if problems:
        return problems, lines
    problems += check_pattern(shots[300])
    problems += check_test_screen(shots[800])
    changed = {y for y in range(240) for x in range(240) if shots[800][y][x] != shots[1500][y][x]}
    if not changed or not changed <= set(BEAT_ROWS):
        problems.append("screen: from 800 to 1 500 ms rows %s changed, not some of the heartbeat's %d to %d only"
                        % (sorted(changed)[:8], BEAT_ROWS[0], BEAT_ROWS[-1]))
    for when, (screen, shown) in ((300, (1, None)), (800, (2, 0)), (1500, (2, 1))):
        b = beacons[when]
        good = consistent(b)
        seconds = good[-1][0] // 1000 if good else None
        lines.append("  %4d ms: screen %d, heartbeat shown %d s, beats %s" % (when, b["screen"], b["shown"],
                                                                            good[-1][0] if good else "?"))
        if b["screen"] != screen:
            problems.append("screen %d ms: the beacon says screen %d, not %d" % (when, b["screen"], screen))
        if shown is not None and (b["shown"] != shown or seconds != shown):
            problems.append("screen %d ms: heartbeat shown %d at %s whole seconds, expected %d"
                            % (when, b["shown"], seconds, shown))
    return problems, lines


def check_flood(case_dir, result, screen_dir):
    """Problems with the flood case (whole frames back to back): every tick
    interval still within INTERVAL_TOL, frames going out, and the picture
    still the test screen; lines with the frame time."""
    with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
        b = beacon(f.read())
    problems, lines = [], []
    n, lo, hi = b["tick_count"], b["interval_min"], b["interval_max"]
    ms = float(result["run"]["emulated_ms"])
    instr = result["run"]["instructions"]["core0"]
    flood = b["frames"] - 2       # the two frames before the flood
    lines.append("  ticks %d, interval %d to %d time base ticks (jitter %d), during %d whole frames"
                 % (n, lo, hi, hi - lo, flood))
    if flood > 0:
        lines.append("  a whole frame: %d time base ticks (%.2f us) from its window to its last transfer"
                     " started; %.0f core-0 instructions a frame over the run"
                     % (b["frame_ticks"], b["frame_ticks"] / 24.0, instr / b["frames"]))
    for name, v in (("shortest", lo), ("longest", hi)):
        if abs(v - TICKS_PER_MS) > INTERVAL_TOL:
            problems.append("flood: %s tick interval %d, not within %d of %d" % (name, v, INTERVAL_TOL, TICKS_PER_MS))
    # The flood starts with the test screen, at 500 ms; a frame is a few
    # microseconds of the core's time in fwtest, so far more frames than
    # ticks go out.
    if n < ms - 2 or flood < 10 * (n - 500):
        problems.append("flood: %d ticks and %d frames in %.3f ms, expected a tick a ms and more than ten"
                        " frames a tick after 500 ms" % (n, flood, ms))
    try:
        _, _, end = read_png(os.path.join(case_dir, "lcd-end.png"))
        _, _, ref = read_png(os.path.join(screen_dir, "lcd-800ms.png"))
        if end != ref:
            problems.append("flood: the picture at the end is not the test screen")
    except (OSError, ValueError) as e:
        problems.append("flood: %s" % e)
    return problems, lines


def build_tests(build):
    """Builds the test images; returns problems."""
    problems = []
    for name, define in sorted(TEST_BUILDS.items()):
        out = os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", "build-" + name)
        p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/build.sh", "build", "--out", out, "--define", define],
                           cwd=ROOT, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            problems.append("%s: the build failed:\n%s" % (name, p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace")[-2000:]))
            continue
        shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(out, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, "out", "fw", name + ".bin"))
        print("built %s (-D%s)" % (name, define))
    return problems


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
    ap.add_argument("--build", required=True, help="a tools/build.sh output folder")
    ap.add_argument("--out", required=True, help="where the suite's outputs go (empty or new)")
    a = ap.parse_args()

    os.makedirs(os.path.join(ROOT, os.path.dirname(IMAGE)), exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copyfile(os.path.join(a.build, "app.bin"), os.path.join(ROOT, IMAGE))
    global START_SLACK
    size = os.path.join(a.build, "app.size")
    if os.path.exists(size):
        with open(size) as f:
            sizes = dict(l.split() for l in f if l.strip())
        print("image size: " + ", ".join("%s %s" % kv for kv in sizes.items()))
        START_SLACK = start_slack(int(sizes.get("bss", 0)))
        print("start slack: %d time base ticks (bss cleared before main starts the time base)" % START_SLACK)
    symbols = elf_symbols(os.path.join(a.build, "app.elf"))
    problems = build_tests(a.build)

    out = os.path.abspath(a.out)
    p = subprocess.run(["sh", "tools/fwtest", "suite", SUITE, "--out", out], cwd=ROOT,
                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
    print(p.stdout.decode("utf-8", "replace").rstrip())
    if p.returncode != 0:
        problems.append("fwtest suite exited %d" % p.returncode)

    steady = {}
    for name in EXPECT:
        path = os.path.join(out, name, "result.json")
        if not os.path.exists(path):
            problems.append("%s: no result.json" % name)
            continue
        with open(path) as f:
            result = json.load(f)
        problems += check_case(name, result)
        run = result.get("run", {})
        print("%s: %s at %s ms, %s instructions on core 0"
              % (name, run.get("outcome"), run.get("emulated_ms"),
                 run.get("instructions", {}).get("core0")))
        for g in result.get("golden") or []:
            print("  golden %s: %s" % (g.get("name"), g.get("result")))
            if g.get("result") != "match":
                problems.append("%s: golden %s: %s" % (name, g.get("name"), g.get("detail")))
        if name in ("boot", "screen", "fault", "stray") and not result.get("golden"):
            problems.append("%s: no golden files compared" % name)
        case_dir = os.path.join(out, name)
        more, lines = [], []
        if name == "boot":
            more, lines = check_boot(case_dir, symbols)
        elif name in ("heartbeat", "heartbeat2") and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_heartbeat(case_dir, result)
            with open(os.path.join(case_dir, "ram-01c00000-%x-end.bin" % BEACON_LEN), "rb") as f:
                steady[name] = (result, beacon(f.read()))
            if len(steady) == 2:
                m, l = check_steady([steady["heartbeat"][0], steady["heartbeat2"][0]],
                                    [steady["heartbeat"][1], steady["heartbeat2"][1]])
                more, lines = more + m, lines + l
        elif name == "screen":
            more, lines = check_screen(case_dir)
        elif name == "flood" and "emulated_ms" in run:
            more, lines = check_flood(case_dir, result, os.path.join(out, "screen"))
        elif name == "fault":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STACK, 1)
        elif name == "stray":
            more, lines = check_halt(name, case_dir, HALT_STRAY, 127)
        problems += more
        if lines:
            print("\n".join(lines))

    for prob in problems:
        print("FAIL: " + prob)
    print("fw suite: %s" % ("FAIL" if problems else "PASS"))
    return 1 if problems else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

### HW-16: TIMER0 to TIMER3
- Fact: In fwtest, `JL_TIMERn->CON` bits 0-1 non-zero run timer n (n = 0
  to 3); `CON` bits 4-7 select a prescaler of the 24 MHz clock. The timer
  counts up from `CNT` and, on reaching `PRD`, raises interrupt source
  4 + n and starts again from 0. `CON` bit 15 reads 1 while pending;
  writing `CON` with bit 14 set clears it. Prescaler setting 2 divides by
  16; the other settings were not measured (Q-3).
- Sources: SDK `hwi.h` lines 42-45 (`IRQ_TIMER0_IDX` 4 to
  `IRQ_TIMER3_IDX` 7); E-3: TIMER0 with prescaler setting 2 and `PRD` 1500
  interrupted every 1 ms (52 by 52.3 ms), and `CON` read `0x8021` in its
  handler (pending, prescaler 2, running).
- Standing: superseded by HW-48
- Needed by: M1

### HW-19: Interrupt source numbers
- Fact: The sources this spec uses: 3 core tick timer, 4-7 TIMER0-3,
  11 the audio link `JL_ALNK0` (the SDK's `IRQ_ALNK_IDX`), 16 SPI1 (LCD),
  24 SARADC, 63 TIMER5, 120-127 software interrupts 0-7. (TIMER4 is
  source 62 on the chip; it never fires in fwtest, HW-14.) The SDK's
  `hwi.h` lists the rest.
- Sources: SDK `hwi.h` lines 41-121.
- Standing: confirmed (SDK)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-20: Enabling a source, and its priority
- Fact: Each core has its own enable and priority words, `ICFG00` to
  `ICFG31`: core 0's at `0x01EEF100` to `0x01EEF17C`, core 1's at
  `0x01EEF300` to `0x01EEF37C`. Source n uses 4 bits of word n / 8, at bit
  position 4 × (n mod 8): bit 0 enables it, bits 1-3 are its priority 0-7.
  A higher number is a higher priority. A source interrupts only the cores
  whose words enable it.
- Sources: SDK `csfr.h` lines 208-214, 280-312; SDK `hwi.h` line 135
  ("0~7, larger is higher"); RE `docs/io/01-boot.md` §4.1 (the 4-bit
  encoding and the two arrays); E-3, E-9 (sources enabled this way).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, RE, E-3)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-21: The global interrupt gates
- Fact: A core takes interrupts only while both gates are open: bit 8 of
  its special register `icfg` (the master enable; not to be confused with
  the `ICFG00`-`ICFG31` words of HW-20) and the enable set by the
  instruction `sti` (cleared by `cli`). At entry `icfg` reads 0, so bit 8
  is clear: set it and execute `sti` before expecting interrupts.
- Sources: SDK `include_lib/driver/cpu/wl82/asm/irq.h` lines 19-21 (bit 8
  of `icfg` as the enable); RE `docs/io/01-boot.md` §4.1, §5.2; E-1
  (`icfg` 0 at entry); E-3 (interrupts taken after setting `icfg` bit 8
  and executing `sti`).
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, RE, E-3)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-22: Entering and leaving a handler, in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest, when a core takes an interrupt the address to return to
  is put in the special register `reti` and the core jumps to the handler;
  the handler returns with `rti`. A handler compiled with the toolchain's
  interrupt function attribute returns correctly. A running handler can be
  interrupted by a pending source of higher priority only after it has
  stored `reti` to its stack, and only until it loads `reti` back; sources
  of the same or lower priority wait until it returns. When several enabled
  sources are pending, the one with the highest priority is taken; between
  equal priorities the order is not specified. fwtest models only core 0's
  tick timer and software-interrupt words (HW-17, HW-23), and one vector
  table for both cores. Whether the chip behaves the same way is Q-10.
- Sources: the emulator model; E-3 and E-9 show only that handlers written
  with the toolchain's interrupt attribute run repeatedly and return.
- Standing: emulator-only
- Needed by: M1

### HW-23: Software interrupts
- Fact: Writing bit b (0-7) to `ILAT_SET` makes source 120 + b pending;
  writing bit b to `ILAT_CLR` clears it. Core 0's are at `0x01EEF1A0` and
  `0x01EEF1A4`, core 1's `0x200` higher (fwtest has core 0's only, HW-22).
  The handler must clear its source, or it is taken again on return.
- Sources: SDK `csfr.h` lines 208-214, 322-323; SDK `cpu.h` line 59 (the
  SDK raises one this way); E-3: `ILAT_SET` bit 0 ran the handler of
  source 120 once, which cleared it.
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, E-3)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-24: Waiting for an interrupt, in fwtest
### HW-48: TIMER0 to TIMER3, and what the acknowledge does in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest, `JL_TIMERn->CON` bits 0-1 non-zero run timer n (n = 0
  to 3); `CON` bits 4-7 select a prescaler of the 24 MHz clock. The timer
  counts up from `CNT` and, on reaching `PRD`, raises interrupt source
  4 + n and starts again from 0. `CON` bit 15 reads 1 while pending;
  writing `CON` with bit 14 set clears it. That acknowledging write also
  restarts the count, from the value last written to `CNT` (0 after an
  interrupt), and the period from the moment of the write. So in fwtest the
  time between
  two interrupts is `PRD` prescaled counts plus the time from the interrupt
  to the write that acknowledges it: with prescaler setting 2 and `PRD`
  1500, 24 000 time-base ticks (HW-13) plus about 1 tick when the handler
  acknowledges first, and more when it acknowledges later. This is fwtest,
  not a firmware setting: the period does not depend on anything but `PRD`,
  the prescaler and where the acknowledge sits. Whether the chip restarts
  the count on the acknowledge is Q-13. On the chip, the SDK names the
  prescaler settings 0 to 15 as dividing by 1, 4, 16, 64, 2, 8, 32, 128,
  256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768; in fwtest only setting 2
  (16) was measured (Q-3). Supersedes HW-16, which said the count starts
  again from 0 on reaching `PRD` without saying what the acknowledge does.
- Sources: SDK `hwi.h` lines 42-45 (`IRQ_TIMER0_IDX` 4 to `IRQ_TIMER3_IDX`
  7); SDK `apps/common/example/peripheral/timer/test2.c` lines 58-75 (the
  prescaler table); E-3 (the 1 ms period, `CON` read `0x8021` in the
  handler); E-13: over 100 periods, 2 400 100 ticks (24 001.0 a period)
  with the acknowledge first in the handler (1 tick after entry), and
  2 408 160 ticks (24 081.6) with it 82 ticks after entry; `CNT` read 5
  just before the acknowledge and 0 just after.
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, E-13)
- Needed by: M1

  writing bit b to `ILAT_CLR` clears it. Core 0's are at `0x01EEF1A0` and
  `0x01EEF1A4`, core 1's `0x200` higher (fwtest has core 0's only, HW-22).
  The handler must clear its source, or it is taken again on return.

  SDK raises one this way); E-3: `ILAT_SET` bit 0 ran the handler of
  source 120 once, which cleared it.
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, E-3)
- Needed by: M1

### HW-24: Waiting for an interrupt, in fwtest
### HW-48: TIMER0 to TIMER3, and what the acknowledge does in fwtest
- Fact: In fwtest, `JL_TIMERn->CON` bits 0-1 non-zero run timer n (n = 0
  to 3); `CON` bits 4-7 select a prescaler of the 24 MHz clock. The timer
  counts up from `CNT` and, on reaching `PRD`, raises interrupt source
  4 + n and starts again from 0. `CON` bit 15 reads 1 while pending;
  writing `CON` with bit 14 set clears it. That acknowledging write also
  restarts the count, from the value last written to `CNT` (0 after an
  interrupt), and the period from the moment of the write. So in fwtest the
  time between
  two interrupts is `PRD` prescaled counts plus the time from the interrupt
  to the write that acknowledges it: with prescaler setting 2 and `PRD`
  1500, 24 000 time-base ticks (HW-13) plus about 1 tick when the handler
  acknowledges first, and more when it acknowledges later. This is fwtest,
  not a firmware setting: the period does not depend on anything but `PRD`,
  the prescaler and where the acknowledge sits. Whether the chip restarts
  the count on the acknowledge is Q-13. On the chip, the SDK names the
  prescaler settings 0 to 15 as dividing by 1, 4, 16, 64, 2, 8, 32, 128,
  256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 512, 2048, 8192, 32768; in fwtest only setting 2
  (16) was measured (Q-3). Supersedes HW-16, which said the count starts
  again from 0 on reaching `PRD` without saying what the acknowledge does.
- Sources: SDK `hwi.h` lines 42-45 (`IRQ_TIMER0_IDX` 4 to `IRQ_TIMER3_IDX`
  7); SDK `apps/common/example/peripheral/timer/test2.c` lines 58-75 (the
  prescaler table); E-3 (the 1 ms period, `CON` read `0x8021` in the
  handler); E-13: over 100 periods, 2 400 100 ticks (24 001.0 a period)
  with the acknowledge first in the handler (1 tick after entry), and
  2 408 160 ticks (24 081.6) with it 82 ticks after entry; `CNT` read 5
  just before the acknowledge and 0 just after.
- Standing: confirmed (SDK, E-13)
- Needed by: M1

content.content:
### 2026-10-22 M1: the vector table and handler conventions
- Facts: HW-18 (the handler of source n is the word at `0x01C7FE00 + 4n`,
  in RAM, written by the firmware; slot 126 is also core 1's start word),
  HW-20 (`ICFG00`-`ICFG31`: enable and priority, 4 bits a source), HW-21
  (both gates: `icfg` bit 8 and `sti`), HW-22 (a handler built with the
  toolchain's interrupt attribute enters and returns correctly; nesting
  only above the running priority; emulator-only), HW-3 (user mode, and an
  interrupt switches to `ssp`; emulator-only). The SDK's `hwi.h` (P-16):
  sources 0 to 2 are the debug, exception and system-call sources, and its
  `irq.h` shows the toolchain's `interrupt("")` attribute.
- Reasoning:
  - Handlers are C functions with the toolchain's `interrupt("")`
    attribute, which saves and restores what it uses (`psr`, `reti` and the
    registers it touches) and returns with `rti`; so the tick is plain C.
  - Every slot is written at startup: source 4 gets `sb_tick`, every other
    source its own 2-byte stub in crt0.S (`call sb_irq_stub_common`, 128
    in source order, 256 bytes). The common code works out the source from
    the return address the call left in `rets` and halts with a report, so
    an unexpected interrupt is named exactly, without reading any pending
    register the spec doesn't describe. The link fails if a stub isn't 2
    bytes. Slot 126 holds a stub like the others: core 1 stays parked (it
    is never released, so its start word is never needed).
  - All 32 `ICFG` words are written, so nothing a loader left enabled stays
    enabled. Only two sources are enabled: the tick at priority 1, and the
    exception source at 7. Nothing else is enabled, so nothing nests; when
    something needs to preempt the tick (M4's audio), priorities are set
    then.
  - Stacks: main runs in user mode on `sp`, interrupts on `ssp` (HW-3),
    each 2 KiB of the 4 KiB stack area, main's on top. `ssp` is set in
    `_start`, before anything could enable an interrupt.
- Experiment (ours, in fwtest): the attribute's code saves `{psr, reti}`
  and `{r5-r0}`, and a handler's `sp` was `ssp` less 32 bytes: so
  interrupts from user mode do run on `ssp`, and user mode may read and
  write `ssp` and `icfg` (HW-3, HW-21 confirmed by our own run). Every one
  of the 128 slots is checked against the image's symbols in the boot case.
- Alternatives: one shared handler for every unexpected source (rejected:
  it couldn't say which); reading `IPND0`-`IPND7` (`csfr.h`) to find the
  source (rejected: not in the spec, and fwtest may not model it); a
  supervisor-mode main on one stack (rejected: the spec doesn't say how to
  enter supervisor mode).

### 2026-10-22 M2: speed in two parts, startup and steady state
- Facts: docs/HARNESS.md ("Time": instruction counts leave out the time a
  waiting core 0 skips; a run's end comes late while the image idles);
  the owner's decision in session M2 (R-PERF-2).
- Reasoning: until M2, speed was one one-second run's instructions over its
  beats, so one-off work at startup counted as if it were per-period work.
  M2 draws the whole screen at startup, hundreds of thousands of
  instructions, which against M1's 69.2 a period would fail the 3% gate
  by design while the per-period work hardly changes. So `tools/perf.py`
  runs each image twice, for 1 250 and 2 250 ms, and takes:
  - steady state: the longer run's instructions less the shorter's, over
    the beats gained between their ends;
  - startup: the shorter run's instructions beyond its beats at that rate.
  Both get a budget per milestone, raised only by their own pull request.
  The 3% gate applies to steady state only, and only against a record
  made under the same steady-state budget: raising that budget is the
  deliberate, reviewed way to accept more work per period.
- Why 1 250 and 2 250 ms: the window between them is one whole second
  long, and both ends are at least 50 ms from a whole tenth of a second
  (a test checks this). Work timed on whole seconds or tenths (M2's
  heartbeat on screen) then falls inside the window whole, never at its
  ends, even though an end comes up to about 30 ms late while the image
  idles. Measured on M1's firmware: the ends came at 1 263.074 and
  2 255.115 ms, 992 beats apart; steady state exactly 64.000 a period
  (the probes' windows, 1 003 and 1 008 beats, gave the same), startup
  5 193 instructions. M1's old figure, 69.2, was the two mixed.
- M1's new budgets: startup 8 192 instructions, steady state 72 a period
  (about 58% and 12% above what M1 measures; the 3% gate, not the budget,
  catches small rises).
- The probes: the slower build must fail the speed gate and the
  unmodified build's steady state as its budget; the bigger build (whose
  extra work runs at startup) must fail each size budget and the
  unmodified build's startup as its budget.
- perf-history.csv keeps its header (its writer refuses any other, and it
  is never rewritten), so its instruction columns now hold the steady
  state, and its `period` column says `heartbeat-steady` from M2 on.
- Alternatives (the owner chose among them): resetting the baseline when a
  milestone's firmware first lands (it hides the startup cost from every
  gate); steady state alone with no startup budget (startup could then
  grow unchecked); one absolute budget for the mixed measure (startup
  would hide per-period regressions).

### 2026-10-22 M2: bringing up the panel
- Facts: HW-27 (an ST7789V-family controller, 16-bit pixels), HW-29 and
  HW-30 (bytes through `BUF`, DMA through `ADR` and `CNT`, PC8 for data or
  command), HW-31 (the commands fwtest acts on), HW-32 and the datasheet
  (P-22: 5 ms after `SWRESET`, 120 ms after one sent in sleep mode before
  `SLPOUT`, 5 ms after `SLPOUT`; `0x3A` `0x55` for 16-bit pixels;
  `MADCTL`'s bits, page 215).
- Our sequence (`lcd_init`, then `main`): software reset; 120 ms, because
  after power-up the controller is in sleep mode, which covers the 5 ms
  too; sleep out; 5 ms; 16-bit pixels; `MADCTL` 0 (rows top to bottom,
  columns left to right, not exchanged, refresh top to bottom, RGB order);
  the first whole frame (the address pattern) while the display is still
  off, so nothing undefined is ever shown; display on. Each delay is
  waited on the tick (`sb_wait_ms` waits one beat more than asked, since
  the first may be nearly over), so it holds on the chip too, where
  fwtest doesn't check it. The 125 ms cost nothing in instructions: the
  core idles.
- What is left out, and why: the panel's reset pin, backlight pin, SPI1's
  clock, mode and pins, and the panel's offset in the controller's
  240 x 320 memory are unknown (Q-6; SR-3 asks). Writing guesses would
  either touch registers fwtest doesn't model (every case fails on an
  unmodelled access) or set the chip up wrongly. `SPI_CON` in `lcd.c` is
  the one place their bits will go. Display inversion isn't sent: whether
  this panel needs it is part of Q-6, and fwtest shows pixels as written
  either way (HW-31). Only bit 8 of `JL_PORTC->OUT` is ever changed, by
  read-modify-write, so M3 can share the port.

### 2026-10-22 M2: the frame buffer and sending it
- Facts: HW-29 (DMA from RAM; a finished transfer can raise source 16;
  E-5 confirms 480-byte transfers), HW-31 (pixels high byte first,
  filling the window row by row), HW-6 (512 KiB of RAM on the chip),
  HW-19 and HW-20 (source 16, priorities).
- Layout: one buffer of the panel's 240 x 240 pixels, row by row from the
  top left, each pixel's RGB565 colour stored high byte first: exactly the
  bytes the panel takes after a memory write, so any run of whole rows is
  one contiguous block DMA can send as it is, with no conversion and no
  copy. 115 200 bytes, in `.bss` (cleared at startup like any zeroed data,
  about 58 000 instructions; the pattern then writes every pixel).
- Sending (`lcd_send_rows`): the window (column and row address set),
  memory write, then the rows by DMA. Up to 16 rows (7 680 bytes) go as
  one transfer whose end the next command polls; more go as a chain of
  16-row chunks, each started by SPI1's interrupt (source 16) when the
  one before ends, so the core is free while a frame goes out. A whole
  frame is 15 chunks. 16 rows is a guess at a safe transfer length: E-5
  confirms 480 bytes, and the chip's limit on `CNT` is asked in SR-3.
- The tick is above SPI1 in priority (1 against 0), and nothing nests, so
  a tick waits at most for one SPI1 handler: about 40 instructions, well
  inside the ±24 time base ticks (240 cycles) the tick's timing allows.
  The flood test (R-LCD-5) sends whole frames back to back for a second:
  every interval stays 24 001 or 24 002.
- Cost: in fwtest a transfer finishes at once (HW-29), so a whole frame
  is only the core's work: 6.3 µs from the window to the last chunk
  started (about 1 000 instructions), recorded as `frame_update_us`. On
  the chip the bytes take time: at the datasheet's fastest serial write
  (66 ns a bit, page 43) a whole frame is at least 921 600 bits, 60.8 ms,
  during which the core is free; the real figure waits for SPI1's clock
  (SR-3).
- fwtest raises source 16 at the end of every DMA transfer while the
  source is enabled, bit 13 or not (our experiment, P-20); HW-29 says bit
  13 enables it. So the handler acknowledges a transfer it didn't chain
  (the polled one) and marks it done, which is right under either
  behaviour; SR-3 reports the difference.
- `lcd_wait` spins rather than idling: an interrupt ending the last chunk
  between the test and an `idle` made the core sleep until the next tick,
  once a frame (the flood test found it: 999 frames a second instead of
  over 200 000). Only a command that must follow a frame still going out
  ever waits.
- Alternatives: 8-bit colour with a palette (57 600 bytes, but every pixel
  converted on the way out, so no straight DMA); two buffers (twice the
  RAM, for tearing-free updates M2 doesn't need); sending a dirty
  rectangle row by row (a transfer per row; the heartbeat is cheaper as
  whole rows, one transfer).

### 2026-10-22 M2: drawing, and our own font
- Fill and frames write two pixels a word where they can; lines step one
  pixel along the longer axis and move along the other when the
  accumulated error passes half a pixel; text writes every pixel of each
  character cell (glyph and background), so text needs no clearing first.
  Everything is clipped to the screen.
- The font is ours (P-21): printable ASCII on a 5 x 8 grid in a 6 x 8
  cell, capitals and digits in rows 0 to 6, descenders in row 7. It is
  written in `font.c` as rows of `#` and `.`, which the compiler folds
  into one byte a row (760 bytes), so anyone can see each glyph in the
  source. Characters outside it draw as a filled box.

### 2026-10-22 M2: the screens, and what they prove
- The address pattern (first): red = column / 8, green = row / 4, blue =
  (column mod 8) x 4 + row mod 4. No two pixels share a colour, so
  fw-suite.py decodes fwtest's capture and checks every one of the 57 600
  pixels against the formula: orientation, colour order and every pixel's
  address at once (R-LCD-2).
- The test screen (from 500 ms): a white border on every edge pixel;
  12 x 12 corner squares, red top left, green top right, blue bottom left,
  yellow bottom right, each named beside it; red, green and blue ramps
  (32, 64 and 32 steps from 0); a box with diagonals and a cross of lines;
  every glyph of the font; the title; the heartbeat. fw-suite.py checks
  the border, corners and ramps pixel by pixel on its own (a mirrored,
  upside-down or BGR picture fails), and the whole picture against a
  golden image (R-LCD-3).
- Captures come late while the image idles (up to about 15 ms here), so
  each screen stays up for hundreds of milliseconds around its capture
  times (300, 800 and 1 500 ms), and the heartbeat changes only on whole
  seconds.

### 2026-10-22 M2: the heartbeat on screen, within 3% a period
- The heartbeat's seconds, five digits at twice the font's size, are
  drawn when a second is up, and only their 16 rows are sent, as one
  transfer: 5.75 µs of the core a second. Only the digits that change are
  drawn again.
- Finding the second without costing a period anything: `main`'s idle
  loop counts its wakes in a register (one a tick: in steady state nothing
  else wakes it) and compares with the next second's count. That is three
  instructions a period, as M1's loop (`idle`, a memory increment, a jump)
  was; a first version that stored the count every time cost one more,
  64 to 65 a period, which with the heartbeat's drawing went over the 3%
  gate (+3.9%). The count goes to the beacon once a second with the ticks
  taken then, so R-IRQ-1 is still checked exactly.
- Result: steady state 65.415 instructions a period against M1's 64.000
  (+2.2%): the heartbeat's drawing and sending, about 1 400 instructions a
  second. Startup 1 036 288 (the two screens and clearing the buffer).

### 2026-10-22 M2: the tests' timing
- The two heartbeat cases differ only in length (1.25 and 2.25 s), so
  their difference is the steady state, as in perf.py; R-IRQ-1's 100
  instructions a tick is checked there, since the whole run's count is now
  mostly startup.
- Startup clears `.bss` before `main` starts the time base, so the time
  base starts about 0.24 ms after fwtest's clock (it was 8 µs). The end
  check's slack now grows with the image's `.bss` (at most 3 cycles a
  word: 2 measured), from `app.size` (P-20).
- The screen case captures the beacon with each picture; the beacon's
  `shown` seconds must equal the heartbeat's whole seconds (R-LCD-4).
